entries.description: Computer-use provider for Duckwork: the stock computer_use tool drives desktop apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the Alan's Way Plugin's workspace setup. Select it with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer (the Alan's Way Plugin's setup.sh sets this when it installs the provider; in the catalog flow it prints the command). Disclosure — starts the workspace router from the profile's mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (command and args from config.yaml, with a filtered environment plus DUCKWORK_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_DESKTOP_ACTIONS=1, which lets this private router child serve desktop input) as a long-running node child per session. The filtered environment passes PATH, HOME, locale and OS basics, plus DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS so the router's VM-desktop fallback finds the X display and session bus, plus DUCKWORK_HOME set to the bound profile's home, under which the router appends a content-free serving log to logs/workspace-router.log; no keys or tokens. It talks to the router over stdio (app lists, element trees, screenshots and input actions). The router reaches the user's computer over SSH on the user's tailnet and falls back to the VM's desktop, where it uses xdotool, a screenshot tool and the AT-SPI accessibility bus if they are installed (the provider installs none of them). On the user's Mac the provider can bring the target app to the front when the model asks for it (focus_app with raise_window, or an input action with delivery_mode foreground), and the Alan's Workspace host does so only after the user has been idle for at least 2 seconds; focus_app can also launch a named app, or open a document or folder by absolute path in its app (the host refuses app bundles, executables, scripts and off-limits apps). Every input action still goes through Duckwork's computer_use approval gate, with raising and foreground input under their own approval scopes (the cua:<action>:background entries in command_allowlist that the Alan's Way Plugin's --allow-desktop-actions adds skip the prompt for background input, focus_app and launches, not for raising or foreground input). The provider itself makes no network calls. On Duckwork 0.21.5, which has no provider API, it installs and does nothing. Since 0.21.0, captures keep element numbers stable across action replies on Mac and Windows, fold in changed controls and report removed numbers; a truncated list never treats unseen controls as removed. Linux keeps the whole-tree generation guard, so capture again before acting by number after a change. Action replies describe nearby changes and can mark the effect confirmed. Default som captures skip the screenshot call entirely when finite snapshot window geometry proves named controls cover at least 35%; older snapshots without geometry still fetch a screenshot to measure coverage and may omit it from the model; mode vision explicitly includes it and mode ax requests no screenshot. Replies identify the coordinate space and explain locked screens, missing permissions, unreadable or cut trees, hung apps and uncertain outcomes before a retry. Captures request generation-based snapshot deltas, validate them against the held tree and retry once for a full list on invalid or mismatched deltas; older apps may return full or unchanged lists. Once a reply identifies a window, later captures, screenshots and input stay bound to that window; capture(window_id=...) selects another. Mismatched window replies clear the target and require a fresh capture. Desktop actions carry expect_host from the observed host so a routing switch refuses input before dispatch; app IDs and element numbers must be reacquired after a switch. Element trees, generation, bound window ID, screenshots' geometry and host OS are session memory, with no new persistent provider state, tools, hooks, middleware, required environment variables or direct network destinations. Duckwork's unmodified CI-pinned scanner reports SAFE: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the long-running router Popen in __init__.py and its bounded 40-second --probe subprocess) and 0 LOW. Browser commit approvals are separate from this provider's unchanged computer_use approval gate.
known_issues: Needs a Duckwork build with the pluggable computer-use API (Duckwork 0.21.6 or newer). On older Duckwork the plugin installs and does nothing. Install alans-way first and run its workspace setup, which writes the workspace_browser block this provider reuses.

Duckwork asks for approval on every computer_use action type until it is granted. For an unattended Telegram bot, grant them once with Always in Telegram, or add cua:<action>:background entries to command_allowlist (see the README). Takes effect after a gateway restart.

The pinned README requires in-process loading and says plugins.isolation: host is unsupported because the provider hands Duckwork a live router session. The current admission validator reports host readiness; remote isolation compatibility has not been verified.

Typing without a target field types into the focused field (still approval-gated). On the user's Mac this needs Alan's Workspace 0.21.9: the target app is brought forward only after the user has been idle for at least 2 seconds, password fields are refused, and the focused field must belong to the target app.

The VM desktop path needs xdotool, a screenshot tool (scrot, maim or ImageMagick import), the AT-SPI bus and python3-gi on the VM. Without them those calls fail and the agent reports it; setup.sh warns about what is missing.

A default som capture skips the screenshot request when snapshot geometry establishes 35% named-control coverage; older apps without geometry still require a screenshot to check it and may omit it from the model. Use mode vision to request it explicitly, or mode ax for an element-only capture. When a screenshot is omitted, coordinate= and element bounds are screen pixels.

Mac and Windows action replies update the held element list without shifting surviving numbers. On Linux, capture again before acting by number after a tree change; cut replies do not prove an unseen control is gone. A timeout or hung app can leave the action's outcome uncertain: capture before retrying.

This release changes provider code: focus_app launches a named app, or opens a document or folder by absolute path in its app on the user's computer (needs Alan's Workspace 0.21.9 with computer-open-v1; app bundles, executables, scripts and off-limits apps are refused). It binds the window showing the opened item. When an action lands on an unfocused window it returns that error and tells the model to ask for a raise explicitly (focus_app with raise_window=true, or delivery_mode='foreground'), which Duckwork approves under its foreground scopes; the provider never raises on its own. It follows the focused window after an app shortcut, and passes the app's step notes to the model. Older apps refuse path opens and keep the earlier behavior.

Admission validation passes with a private-import warning: __init__.py uses tools.mcp_tool_config._resolve_stdio_command to resolve the router launcher; this internal helper may change across Duckwork releases.
entries.name: alans-way-computer
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin: Computer Use

entries.description: Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a Duckwork gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through Duckwork's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store the bound chat's activity timestamps in plugin state; optional cross-bot export adds the separate storage disclosed below. On first load it reads $DUCKWORK_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and hand a JSON setup plan to the human in Alan's Workspace. The app runs setup.sh through an external SSH process outside the gateway, checks the exact repoRef and desktopRef and rejects tracked checkout changes; the agent must never run setup or even --verify in its gateway terminal or bypass the lifecycle guard. Windows guests require the human's external Git Bash shell. The human pastes the app's output for review. The external setup does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units duckwork-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit duckwork-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the duckwork-gateway unit. Duckwork refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or duckwork gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or duckwork gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp_servers.workspace_browser block with connect_timeout: 25 seconds (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser only skips disabling it; it does not re-enable a previously disabled toolset), turns computer_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The skill's moved-VM checklist has the agent read the app's preferences.json on the user's computer over the same SSH path and tell the human where the VNC password lives without pasting it. The Alan's Workspace setup page has the human run the alans-way connect script from its main branch on their own computer, and the agent may install Tailscale with its official install script. The manual --allow-desktop-actions setup flag, which the skill offers but never adds itself, adds cua:*:background entries to command_allowlist. On a Duckwork without the computer-use provider API, including 0.21.5, it also exposes workspace_computer_action, which drives the user's desktop, Terminal included, with no approval. The repo also holds bootstrap-orgo.sh and migrate.sh, which the plugin, setup.sh and the skills never run: a user runs them by hand to provision a fresh supervisord Linux computer (it fetches the Duckwork and Tailscale installers over HTTPS, pipes setup.sh from this repo's main branch into bash unless --repo-ref is given, installs openssh-server if absent, writes supervisord programs, and POSTs the Tailscale login URL with a shared secret to a --callback URL when one is given) or to copy ~/.duckwork, including .env, auth.json and state.db, to another host over SSH (it also looks up each profile's bot username at api.telegram.org with that profile's bot token). Since 0.21.0, every enabled profile also gets a default-on Telegram texting voice: an additional pre_llm_call hook reads that profile's voice mode and adds a tone note to Telegram turns, and transform_llm_output can remove a known leading assistant opener from the final Telegram reply. Messages containing backticks, quotes, indentation or silence markers are left unchanged by that polish. /tone texting|default|status and duckwork tone store the mode under voice in Duckwork plugin state; setup.sh --tone applies it to each configured profile. It layers over the user's persona without writing SOUL.md or agent.system_prompt. Check-ins now name one concrete open thread. /proactivity now requests one immediately from the bound chat even when paused or outside active hours, without changing the settings or unanswered-check-in count. Morning briefs are off by default: /proactivity brief on (or the operator CLI) enables one daily internal user-role prompt near active_start, with 0-20 minutes of jitter, at most two hours late and skipped after recent user activity. It asks the model to consult calendar and email read-only if those tools exist. The existing proactivity tool may disable the brief but cannot enable it; settings.morning_brief and last_brief_date are stored in the existing idle plugin state. The workspace router adds a commit object to the existing browser open/action tools for purchases, bookings, sends, posts, submissions, deletions and account changes. It checks control names, selectors, refs, action-looking URLs, batches, scripts, keys and dialogs against page state; missing page knowledge needs a snapshot or explicit commit. Shared commit-name patterns allow benign Buy it again, Book a demo and Subscribe & Save labels without excusing other commit-bearing words. Tax schedule names are treated as benign labels without exempting one-on-one bookings from approval. It asks through MCP elicitation (60-second default wait, configurable with DUCKWORK_ROUTER_APPROVAL_MS), refuses unavailable, declined, timed-out or stale approvals, drops agent-supplied approval receipts and adds a single-use receipt bound to the approved tab and epoch. An approved commit is never replayed after a lost connection or host change. It appends commit decisions to commit-decisions.jsonl beside the mac-watch state file, creating the log with mode 0600: timestamp, bot id, page origin, decision and any supplied kind, summary, amount, currency and counterparty, or the detected target. Page/control/challenge and pending-approval state is held in memory. The same two skills now prefer Duckwork web_search/web_extract for plain lookups and the user's computer for interactive search, hand CAPTCHAs to the human, poll at most every 30 seconds for up to 30 minutes, and switch sources after two challenges in ten minutes. The router stops remembering challenge pages for failover and reports changed tab ids in result metadata. The operations skill covers the app's automatic takeover after its grace period; CAPTCHA and recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still keep the bot out. It asks the agent to save only lasting general facts and preferences to memory; procedures belong in skills and project/task records in the user's chosen file or tracker, asking where if none is chosen. Existing memory is not migrated or deleted, and live tab state is never saved there. The setup skill pins the companion app source to f110115ff23367e4e21eeaf00e658a8706369652 and adds a long-chat reference: report effective compression and summary routing read-only, then only with explicit consent for each profile enable compression.proactive_prune_tokens at 48000, with 8000-character eligibility and 4096-token minimum reclaim, using the profile-scoped config CLI and keeping custom values, micro_compact and summary routing. This writes the approved profile's config.yaml and records prior values outside the repo for undo; setup.sh does not run it. A weekly time-saved report is a user-created Duckwork cron recipe, not an installed job. setup.sh --verify now checks the running service manager, display, SSH ProxyCommand and managed browser's loopback /json/version endpoint, and reports noVNC reachability from its actual bind address. Manual supervisord restart guidance drains with USR1 first. The repo also adds scripts/voice_eval.py, user-run only: it sends fixed fictional scenarios and replies to Anthropic models through the SDK or claude -p for scoring and optionally writes a JSON result; the plugin, setup and skills never run it. Since 0.21.5, the plugin registers two more bundled skills, web-errands and integrations, with no new tools, hooks, commands or required environment variables. web-errands is guidance for shopping, booking, applications, filings, cancellations and claims in the workspace browser: every purchase, booking, send, submission and deletion still goes through the commit approval gate described above, CAPTCHA, sign-in and card-entry walls go back to the human, and card numbers are never stored. It has the agent record each application's company, role, date, posting URL and confirmation in the user's chosen project/task record, asking where if none is chosen. For a price, restock or status watch the user asks for or explicitly accepts, it has the agent create a Duckwork cron job with Duckwork's cronjob_manage tool (or ask the operator), polling no more often than every 10 minutes and stopping after three consecutive failures; cron runs cannot answer approvals, so a watch that reaches its target stages the result for the user. Watches use attach_to_session: true with no deliver override and continuity: true; each check is a fresh session, uses its prior completed output as a baseline and replies [SILENT] unless something meaningful changed, failed or reached its target. An optional safe read-only deterministic monitor URL or script can skip the model and delivery on unchanged output; probe errors still need reporting/backoff. Cron cannot pause/remove itself unless the operator enabled cron.allow_agent_scheduling. In-chat monitoring is a separate user-entered /heartbeat every command, one per conversation replacing the previous one; it runs only while idle with the chat process/gateway alive, costs a model turn per check and needs /heartbeat clear from the user. The integrations skill has the agent check that an account is connected, with a small read, before promising a task that needs it, and reuses Duckwork's Google Workspace, Himalaya, Home Assistant, Honcho and X routes first. The Google route uses Duckwork's own setup, whose fixed scope list includes write access; the skill says so and stops if the user declines. Only after the user agrees in chat does it guide an install: a Duckwork catalog plugin (Home Assistant or Honcho), a separately reviewed Himalaya v1.2.0 binary, rclone v1.75.2 (the release zip from downloads.rclone.org, checked against that release's SHA256SUMS before extraction) or Taskwarrior 3.5.0 (a source build of upstream commit 3419d5ba1e6a780fbbb0a8d68d8fd31e675c1bf8 cloned from GitHub, after checking the CMake and Rust versions and asking before changing any toolchain), the last two into versioned directories under ~/.local/share/alans-tools/. Secrets are entered by the human in a private terminal outside the agent session, never in Telegram; where a recipe needs a secret in the agent's terminal (a mail credential, RCLONE_CONFIG_PASS), it explains the grant and adds only that variable to the profile's terminal.env_passthrough. The recipes keep rclone.conf (mode 0600) and Taskwarrior's taskrc and data under the profile's DUCKWORK_HOME/integrations. Scheduled reads are read-only cron jobs with a profile-local failure-count file, and pausing goes through the owner conversation or an explicitly authorized duckwork cron pause. API writes (send, post, delete, share) need fresh explicit approval in the live conversation, and a declined, timed-out or unavailable browser commit is never completed through another tool. Mastodon is not bundled: its recipe is human-run documentation in this repo (docs/integrations/mastodon.md) that the plugin and skills never run. None of this runs at plugin load or from setup.sh. Telegram replies, check-ins and briefs share one status-first style: concrete status, evidence or caveat, plain limits, and no tool names, file paths, scripts or job and session IDs in user-facing text unless asked. Prices, availability and policies must come from a page read this turn or be labeled unconfirmed. Multi-step browser work continues in short chunks until done or blocked, with one short start line and one-line updates only at milestones, routed-around failures or noticeable waits; routine reads, actions and transitions stay quiet, a new mid-task message is acknowledged and folded in, and Duckwork's clarify buttons may be used for decisions the user owns, never for approvals; a whole checkout batch still sits under one commit. For a message of 200 characters or fewer that is wholly a recap request, greeting, thanks or acknowledgment, the voice hook appends a three-sentence limit; the check reads only the current message, with no model call, history or network. The check-in menu now ends with asking about a decision the user owns. The operations skill adds tab hygiene: the agent closes finished tabs it owns with the existing close tool, never another bot's or the user's and never one with a pending handback or recording hold. The router adds requestingBotId to tab-list replies and forwards a reply over 4 MiB unchanged, without that decoration, writing a content-free line to stderr. The skill also tells the agent to report installed versions by running duckwork --version, reading the plugin's install metadata, running local git describe and rev-parse on the Alan's Tools checkout, and calling the app's existing status tool. setup.sh --bind now also makes the bound DM Duckwork's Telegram home by running duckwork -p PROFILE config set for TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID (30-second limit each; on failure it warns to send /sethome); it loads on gateway restart. setup.sh --verify exits 0 for a complete local audit, 1 for failed required checks and 2 for a partial install (warnings, or skipped browser or services). The setup skill's checkout step now initializes ~/alans-way-agents if absent and fetches the pin (depth 1) from the repo's GitHub origin, or reuses a clean clone there after two read-only local git helpers (5-second limit) confirm one recorded and effective origin URL naming this repo; for file and direct Git installs it uses the installer-recorded revision, and it never falls back to a tag when that record is invalid. Its computer-use API probe separates an absent API from a failed or timed-out probe and ends the probe's process group or tree on timeout. The setup skill also offers, each only after an explicit answer, with readback and a remembered-choice marker in the profile's config: one grouped autonomy choice for display.busy_input_mode: steer and agent.intent_ack_continuation: true, for every platform in that profile after restart. It reads effective values, including defaults, proposes changes only from stock interrupt/auto and preserves deliberate choices, custom or unknown values and unreadable config. General setup/proactivity consent is insufficient; an explicit no preserves both settings, silence writes nothing. Both keys are read back, including unchanged keys, before writing and reading back skills.config.workspace-setup.autonomy_choice as chosen or keep-current. Failed writes/readbacks leave the marker untouched; it records the answer only and never restores settings. Legacy busy_input_choice: keep-interrupt skips only the busy key; unknown legacy state is reported and skipped. agent.verify_on_stop is left alone unless the coding user requests stricter checks and one grouped Telegram question covering platforms.telegram.typing_indicator, display.platforms.telegram.interim_assistant_messages, tool_progress, notifications, long_running_notifications and busy_steer_ack_enabled, platforms.telegram.reactions, display.memory_notifications (hides the Memory updated and Self-improvement review notices on every platform in that profile), cron.wrap_response (profile-wide: removes scheduled-message headers, job IDs and footers for all delivery targets) and, as a separate city-confirmed question, timezone. Markers written through the same CLI are skills.config.workspace-setup.autonomy_choice and telegram_feel_choice; the former busy_input_choice is read but no longer written; a legacy busy_steer_ack_choice marker is only read, never written. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install, SAFE requires no scanner confirmation; setup and dependency consent remain separate. A later CAUTION revision needs review and explicit consent to the exact tree before retrying duckwork plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --enable alone does not confirm a warning, and --force confirms CAUTION and can replace an install but cannot override DANGEROUS. Duckwork's unmodified scanner reports SAFE for this plugin: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the two git helpers in skills/workspace-setup/SKILL.md) and 3 LOW (hardcoded_ip_port: the loopback forward examples in the same file). This pin also extends the existing texting-note and minimal final-opener polish to public session source tags desktop, tui and bot_room, alongside Telegram; CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources keep their default voice. A tone-independent pre_llm_call task note asks the agent to track and verify mini goals with Duckwork's todo tool or working context, continue independent authorized work through completion, recheck historical blockers against newer messages and verify every requested criterion with each item's own source before replying. It requests a short start line and milestone-only updates, keeps routine work quiet and preserves questions, approvals, failures and honest completion. Recap replies are capped at three sentences total including any detail offer. Follow-up cron jobs are saved only after the user asks or says yes, attached to this chat with attach_to_session: true and no deliver override; no later message may be promised without a saved job. A not-yet reply allows one offer at a named local time, with no saved repeat until consent, and jobs are removed when their reason ends. /goal is suggested once for a big multi-step job, not small asks. Fixed Duckwork progress/error/approval messages are unchanged. Scripted tool conversations prove hook delivery; consistent real-model quiet behavior is unverified. Browser guidance starts normal work in the user's Workspace even while they are away; host vm is for explicit VM requests or router-reported outages, never login/CAPTCHA/approval errors. Existing VM tasks finish there when the computer returns; no third-tier browser is substituted. Reasoned human handbacks hold VM tabs as well as computer tabs for up to 30 minutes until Give back; a chat reply alone cannot bypass awaiting_human. Resume uses the host, tab ID and fresh epoch from one reply. The human-only Move button can carry URL/scroll and chosen drafts; cookies move only when a restore is reported, while passwords, uploads and in-memory state stay behind, and the agent has no move tool. Router changes bind approvals to exact observed page targets, reject missing/malformed action success receipts, bound recovery and owned-child shutdown, and project agent-facing replies without exposing internal approval proof. The router never replays a sent write after connector retry, timeout or host change, including writes before the first response; only reads and unsent calls can replay within their original remaining budget. Cancellation is forwarded and stale-host checks reject queued desktop input before sending it; uncertainty requires checking the outcome before any repeat. Browser and desktop replies add a content-free diagnostic, on stderr and appended to the profile's logs/workspace-router.log, with fixed tool name, serving host, default/request/fallback selection and reason, and elapsed time; it contains no URLs or page/task content. Idle direct SSH probes can discover a recovered computer sooner without moving an active VM task. Cross-bot proactivity adds the cross_bot_ask tool and pre_tool_call/on_session_end hooks; no middleware, required secrets or direct network destinations are added. Optional cross-bot proactivity is off by default, configured with the same explicit absolute shared root and designated primary in each participating profile, then enrolled per bot through /proactivity cross on (activation in a running gateway needs a restart). Only completed user/final-assistant exchanges from each enrolled bot's bound owner Telegram DM are exported: at most four recent exchanges and 2 KiB per digest, expiring after 24 hours per exchange. There is no historical backfill or export of groups, other chats, attachments, reasoning, tool history, cron, check-ins, briefs, child or imported turns. Exchanges that appear to contain credentials or payment details, or match operator redact terms, are skipped entirely before truncation; sanitization cannot detect every secret. Only the designated primary receives other enabled profiles' fresh digests during permitted check-ins, including user-requested /proactivity now; its own digest is excluded and exports are JSON-escaped as untrusted observations, bounded to 32 KiB across 16 profiles. Ordinary turns receive no digests or dispatch permit; separately consented helper results can arrive there as disclosed below. Briefs and cron receive neither. The primary may automatically schedule one read_only or draft_only cross_bot_ask with fresh target evidence per check-in into another enrolled bot's existing bound DM; replies appear there with primary attribution, and only separately consented short outcomes can return to the primary. The receiver needs its own gateway-injection permission and verified routing, observes pause/hours/busy settings, and starts no spontaneous secondary check-ins. Queued asks are at most 800 characters, expire after two hours and are deleted before injection; sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed, with no replay, delivery-receipt store or result polling. Result sharing is separately off by default, including for existing cross-bot users: /proactivity cross results on must be chosen in both bound owner DMs. Only future asks can return a sanitized Done/Blocked summary of at most 280 UTF-8 bytes, correlated to one ask, with the same two-hour expiry measured from ask creation. The private shared results.json stores up to 64 pending/running/completed records with profile identities, enrollment generations, ask IDs, timestamps, prompt/session-correlation hashes, status and summary. Results are consumed once before exposure at the primary's next ordinary owner turn or permitted check-in, as untrusted helper reports rather than independently verified facts. There is no wake, retry or delivery guarantee; a crash or helper restart can lose an outcome. /proactivity cross results off purges pending outcomes; cross off also revokes the choice. Copied outcomes can persist in chat/provider context after expiry or opt-out. Attempts are limited to four per rolling day gateway-wide, two per target and 60-minute target spacing. The plugin-owned POSIX shared directory uses mode 0700 and files 0600: digests and queued bodies, persistent enrollment/generation and eligibility/heartbeat records, body-free turn/attempt hashes retained for 48 hours, one-use check-in permits and imported-session locks expiring within 30 minutes. Session locks contain the exact session key and ask ID and survive restart until session end, expiry or opt-out. Pruning runs on activated startup, before store access and every 60 seconds while connected; offline expired files can remain until an activated profile prunes them. Dormant profiles do no cross-bot store access. /proactivity cross off immediately stops sharing, receiving and dispatch and purges that profile's digest, permits, locks and pending asks; body-free records remain until expiry and scheduler roles revert on restart. Only the operator can enable or expand sharing; the model may disable it. Launch-gateway profile routing policy is read through public configuration/home-scope APIs; no Duckwork session DB or credential store is read for export. Imported sessions block terminal/code, desktop actions, delegation, messaging, scheduling, further cross-bot asks and unknown connectors; reviewed reads/drafting and existing gated browser actions remain allowed. Browser approval, CAPTCHA and ownership gates still apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Copied context goes through the configured model provider and target Telegram delivery and may remain in Duckwork history, API-content sidecars, compaction and memory-provider records, including Honcho when configured, and model-provider retention after expiry or opt-out. The instruction not to save other bots' excerpts is model policy, not enforced deletion; the plugin performs no memory-provider writes. No new direct network endpoint or telemetry is introduced. Optional integrations use the user's selected Google Workspace API, IMAP/SMTP mail service, Home Assistant instance, Honcho API, X API or rclone cloud/WebDAV/S3 endpoint; browser errands contact user-selected sites. Honcho can receive conversation turns, derived conclusions, peer/session IDs and version/OS/plugin headers. Native tools retain their own profile-scoped credentials, including Google client/token/pending OAuth files and encrypted rclone provider tokens; the plugin does not create a separate credential store. Setup downloads also reach GitHub/raw.githubusercontent.com, the official Tailscale installer, configured distro package repositories and the npm/Playwright distribution, in addition to Google and rclone downloads already disclosed.
known_issues: Install this on the machine that runs Duckwork (a Linux host or a macOS guest VM), not on the user's primary computer. Windows guests are new and untested on real hardware. If the plugin is already installed from the catalog, setup leaves it as it is, so this pin stays.

Setup turns off Duckwork's stock browser toolset for Telegram and cron so the agent uses the workspace browser (pass --keep-browser to skip disabling it; this does not re-enable it). It never turns off computer_use: on Duckwork with the computer-use provider API, desktop input goes through the gated computer_use tool and its alans-way-computer provider.
Check-ins need plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection: true and a bound Telegram DM (setup does both). A background thread checks every 60 seconds once the gateway connects Telegram.

Setup may install Chrome, Chromium, Playwright's Chromium or Xvfb with root or passwordless sudo, and may drain-stop and start the profile's gateway to apply a plugin change Duckwork refuses while it runs. Pass --skip-services to skip the services and their packages.
The computer's SSH key is only accepted from the tailnet (from= restriction). An existing unrestricted line for the same key is rewritten with it.
A copy of the workspace-operations skill under a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's and never gets its updates. Setup only warns; move anything worth keeping out of it, then delete it.

The texting voice is default-on for Telegram, desktop, TUI and bot_room source tags. /tone default disables its note and final-opener polish per profile. CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources retain the default voice. Check-ins and morning briefs keep their own short style. Fixed Duckwork progress/error/approval messages, direct sends and cron reports are outside these hooks; interim messages get the tone note but no polish, and streaming can show raw chunks before a final edit. Consistent real-model quiet behavior remains unverified.

Morning briefs are opt-in (/proactivity brief on), use the existing bound DM and gateway-injection permission, and may read calendar/email through tools already available to the model. /proactivity now is user-only from that chat and bypasses pause/hours for one requested check-in.

Telegram browser Approve buttons need Duckwork v0.21.6 or newer including commit 239740a19e (first in date tag v2026.6.19), despite the generic >=0.21.5 install floor. Without MCP form elicitation support commits fail with approval_unavailable; unattended cron declines them. The gate protects against agent mistakes and malicious pages, not a deliberately hostile bot with same-user terminal/file access.

The router appends approval details and detected targets to commit-decisions.jsonl beside mac-watch state, shared by routers using that path; no retention or rotation is implemented. Keep this local log private. CAPTCHA handback, recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still block takeover. If the router reports human_has_control before a commit approval, wait or claim the tab through the normal app control flow first.

Long-chat pruning is an agent-guided, separately consented config option per profile, not a setup.sh default. It preserves customized values and summary routing, rewrites sent history and can break the prompt-cache prefix; undo affects future pruning and cannot restore tool bodies already pruned from active context.

web-errands and integrations are agent guidance, not setup steps. Any Himalaya, rclone, Taskwarrior, Home Assistant or Honcho install happens only after the user agrees in chat, never from setup.sh or plugin load. Taskwarrior is built from source (CMake >=3.24, Rust >=1.91.1 and several GiB of temporary space). The Google Workspace route requests Duckwork's fixed scope list, which includes write access.

Guided setup can change a profile's busy-input, intent-ack continuation, Telegram display, notification, reaction, memory-notice, cron-wrapping and timezone settings, but only after explicit answers. Busy mode, intent-ack continuation, memory-notice hiding, cron.wrap_response and timezone reach beyond Telegram within that profile; the autonomy choice takes effect after restart and preserves existing deliberate choices. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing; neither setup script writes these keys.

setup.sh --bind also sets TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL for the bound profile through duckwork config set and clears TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID; it loads on gateway restart. If that fails, send /sethome in the primary DM.

Desktop control needs a Duckwork with tools.computer_use.backend.ComputerUseProvider (commit 63f5e0ea45726c5d8d7d207d140613997730aab3 or newer); a version string alone does not prove it. setup.sh --verify exits 2, not 0, for a partial install.

This pin needs the paired workspace/remote browser host with approval-binding-v1 support for approved browser actions. Older hosts fail closed when that proof is unavailable; update and verify the paired workspace before rollout.

Cross-bot proactivity is off by default and requires operator configuration and per-bot /proactivity cross on; activation needs a gateway restart. It exports bounded completed owner-DM excerpts across enabled profiles on one gateway. /proactivity cross off stops sharing/receiving/dispatch immediately and purges local shared text and permits; body-free hashes remain for 48 hours. Sanitization skips credential/payment-looking exchanges but cannot guarantee secrecy. Digest TTL is 24 hours, queued asks two hours; offline expired files remain until an activated profile prunes them. Copied context in Duckwork history, sidecars, compaction, memory-provider records and model-provider retention is not erased by expiry or opt-out. The no-memory instruction is model policy. Shared storage requires POSIX owner-only directories/files. Dormant profiles do no store access.

During a permitted primary check-in the model may automatically schedule one read-only/draft-only ask into an enrolled target bot's existing owner DM, with primary attribution. sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed; there is no delivery receipt or replay. A separate off-by-default results opt-in in both owner DMs permits one sanitized summary (280 UTF-8 bytes) per future ask, held in private results.json for at most two hours from the ask and consumed once at the primary's next owner turn or permitted check-in. There is no wake/retry; missing means unknown. Result opt-out purges pending outcomes and cross opt-out revokes the choice; already copied chat/provider context remains. Imported-session restrictions last at most 30 minutes and survive restart; terminal/code, desktop input, delegation, messaging, scheduling and unknown connectors are blocked, while existing gated browser calls remain possible. Existing approval/CAPTCHA/ownership gates apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Targets require gateway-injection permission and verified same-bot routes; missing permission, routing, busy/pause/hours or expiry can prevent delivery.

Admission validation passes with warnings: cross_bot_ask is declared but only registers for an activated primary cross-bot profile; the default isolated probe does not activate it. proactivity.py and voice.py read gateway.session_context.get_session_env, which current Duckwork flags as private imports that may break across releases.

0.21.9 router changes: when the computer's ssh link drops and mac-watch reports it online, the router reconnects to it at most once a minute, re-initializes and replays only read-only and never-sent calls; an action that may already have run is answered as uncertain, never repeated. Only a failed reconnect or an offline/stale computer fails over to the VM, and after a failover a call that names a computer tab is refused rather than served by the VM. The approval gate also learns page names from a tab-open snapshot. A pre_llm_call note on every turn names the workspace tools and routine Mac moves.
entries.name: alans-way
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin

entries.description: Private Yandex Alice voice input for Duckwork, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.
known_issues: Default profile and one existing authorized Telegram DM session only; a private Alice skill and operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy are required.
Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram connect factory receives the native Application and is not supported by plugins.isolation: host.
The webhook URL contains a bearer secret. Yandex request signatures are not verified; body skill/account IDs are not cryptographic authentication.
Alice acknowledges asynchronous scheduling, not completion or delivery. Replies are sent to Telegram, not spoken by Alice.
Deduplication is bounded and memory-only; no durable queue, exactly-once guarantee, or built-in global rate limiter.
entries.name: alice-voice
entries.title: Alice Voice Input

entries.description: Ample (ample.computer) as native tools: deploy the websites and web apps Duckwork builds to public HTTPS URLs, release changes to the same URLs, read build and runtime logs, list and delete apps; bundled skill ample:web-apps. Disclosure — maintained by Ample, the hosting service it deploys to; talks to Ample's API (https://api.ample.computer); on first use downloads the pinned Ample CLI 0.1.36 from Ample's release server (https://get.ample.computer/releases/0.1.36/, SHA-256 checked, never self-updated; cli_path uses your own binary instead) and runs it as a subprocess with an allowlisted environment and its crash reports off; ample_deploy uploads the folder it is given (home, Duckwork home and credential directories refused) and writes ample.toml and .ample/ into it; with no AMPLE_CLIENT_ID/AMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET or AMPLE_TOKEN set, the first deploy signs up for a free Ample account (deleted after two days unless claimed) and saves its credential in Duckwork's .env. A pre_tool_call hook sends every delete (scoped to that app) and the first publish of each folder to Duckwork's approval gate; only folders the user has published, recorded in plugin state, skip it. No telemetry, no background processes.
entries.name: ample
entries.title: Ample

entries.description: Native Anatomy community gallery with search, local favorites and explicit sandboxed standalone playback. Disclosure — when opened it fetches gallery metadata and thumbnails from a third-party GitHub repository (wheresryan22/anatomy-community, resolved at runtime from its mutable previews branch via api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com). "Open figure in Duckwork" downloads that community figure's HTML and runs its JavaScript inside the Desktop SDK sandbox (opaque origin, scripts only), and "Browse Ryan's website" embeds skills.wheresryan.sh the same way. Favorites and filters stay in Desktop-local plugin storage; no credentials or Duckwork data are sent.
known_issues: Requires the matching native Desktop SDK; tested source-built Desktop reports 0.0.0, not a certified prebuilt release number.
Full embedded website navigation and website-wrapper Play-with-it are unsupported; repository standalone playback and external recovery are separate.
Wankel, Zipper and WebGL Ripple tank were interaction-tested; the other catalog figures were not individually certified.
entries.name: anatomy-museum
entries.title: Anatomy Museum

entries.description: Connect a Duckwork agent through an existing Ando invitation and receive authorized messages. Disclosure — connects outbound to Ando (mcp.ando.so, api.ando.so, realtime.ando.so) with an agent API key stored at $DUCKWORK_HOME/ando/connection.json (mode 600); Ando messages from the connecting member (or members the operator explicitly allowlists) start Duckwork turns and the final reply, with any files it attaches, is posted back to Ando; message attachments are uploaded and downloaded through short-lived single-use links Ando issues (up to 20 MB each; received files are cached in the profile's Duckwork cache); duckwork ando connect edits gateway.platforms.ando in config.yaml.
entries.name: ando-platform

entries.description: Control a headless Android emulator from Duckwork — live sidebar, app management, GPS/battery/network simulation, and ADB tools. Emulator host is Linux. Disclosure — requires a pre-installed Android SDK under ~/Android/Sdk; runs adb, emulator, avdmanager and sdkmanager on the host, and the dashboard's Create AVD action downloads Android system images from Google via sdkmanager. emu_shell runs arbitrary commands inside the emulator; emu_install/emu_push copy host files into it.
entries.name: android-emulator

entries.description: Signed messaging with paired Duckwork and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).
entries.name: antenna
entries.title: Antenna for Duckwork

entries.description: Run Duckwork on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, Duckwork tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to Duckwork. Fails closed on any non-Duckwork tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).
entries.name: antigravity-agy

entries.description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `duckwork auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx duckwork-antigravity-oauth`) and run Duckwork on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Duckwork SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Duckwork tool, which then runs under Duckwork approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Duckwork system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).
entries.name: antigravity-oauth

entries.description: Run Duckwork on an Antigravity subscription via the official agy CLI (DirectSDK path). Streams tokens progressively, persists multi-turn trajectories via agy --conversation (up to 239k tokens), discovers models dynamically per account, maps thinking effort, reports quota in /usage, and aborts reported native tools. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list). Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.
entries.name: antigravity-subscription-directsdk

entries.description: AnyAPI.ai — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool results and ANYAPI_API_KEY to api.anyapi.ai, a third-party relay (AnyAPI Inc.) that forwards them to the upstream vendor serving the chosen model; billed to your AnyAPI account.
entries.name: anyapi
entries.title: AnyAPI.ai

entries.description: AnyRouter — unified model gateway (OpenAI-compatible); /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes, first-party meta-models like anyrouter/duckwork. Disclosure — sends your prompts and ANYROUTER_API_KEY to anyrouter.dev, a third-party relay that forwards to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, …), on some plans through a shared pool of other members' donated free-tier vendor keys; billed in prepaid AnyRouter credits. anyrouter/duckwork is AnyRouter's own routing meta-model, not a Fordex model. Opt-in ANYROUTER_APP_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds Duckwork attribution headers.
entries.name: anyrouter

entries.description: AnySearch web search and extraction plus two real-time fallback chains: when a primary backend fails (Exa quota, Firecrawl timeout), the same call is served by AnySearch (1,000 free requests/day).
entries.name: anysearch

entries.description: CCR compression plugin - 28-type classifier, 13 tools, opt-in context engine, TOML-driven templates. Disclosure - pre_tool_call auto-backgrounds long terminal/process commands (modify: background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and rewrites chained terminal commands when enabled. Disclosure — hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_duckwork + aphrodite proxy, v1.6.6) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl…) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the Duckwork home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com).
entries.name: aphrodite

entries.description: Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to DUCKWORK_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential DUCKWORK_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through Duckwork secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after Duckwork read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Duckwork write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.
known_issues: Conflicts with artifact-relay because both register artifact_publish. Enable only one of these plugins.

entries.description: AtmoRouter — OpenAI-compatible gateway; one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Grok models, with the /model picker fed by the live GET /v1/models catalog. Disclosure — sends your prompts, conversation history, tool definitions, tool results and ATMOROUTER_API_KEY to atmorouter.dev, which forwards each request to the upstream infrastructure serving the chosen model; that infrastructure's location and retention vary per model and zero retention is not promised (AtmoRouter states it keeps metadata, not prompt or response content, in its usage records and does not train on API content; https://atmorouter.dev/privacy). Usage is billed per token from a prepaid AtmoRouter balance (USDC on Solana or QRIS); prices vary by capacity tier and a request can route to any listed tier, including tiers above official pricing, unless you set maximum prices under Budgets; failed upstream requests are not billed and the plugin itself makes no payments.

entries.description: Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. It reads public posts and profiles from the Bluesky social media network, which is built on the AT Protocol (atproto), without signing in. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key, and no program on your machine. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with duckwork tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. duckwork author-feed schedule creates one cron job, a model turn every hour by default (two or more model requests, no daily cap). Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run duckwork author-feed unschedule before removal. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with duckwork cron remove <id>. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Duckwork parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall.
entries.name: author-feed

entries.description: Automatically pin every new interactive session (desktop, CLI, TUI) and the branches you fork from them. entries.description: Local ledger of Duckwork's auxiliary LLM calls (titling, compression, vision, approval): /aux shows tokens, time and failures per task, model, provider or day, or lists the newest calls (ten, or up to 100 with /aux recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded. entries.description: @b64: context references that decode encoded text for the model: @b64:<value> takes base64 (standard or URL-safe, padded or not), hex (0x48656c6c6f, 48:65:6c, \x48\x65), percent-encoding or a data: URI, told apart by the value's shape or picked with base64:, base64url:, hex: or url:, and attaches what it holds: text as text with control and invisible characters escaped, JSON pretty-printed, gzip and zlib inflated in memory (at most 1 MiB, one layer), and binary named by its format (PNG and GIF with their size, JPEG, PDF, ZIP, ELF, SQLite and more) with a hex dump of its first 128 bytes; notes point out a value that was cut short, padding that is off, a second layer of encoding and a JWT inside; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's base64, json, urllib.parse and zlib; nothing decoded is run, opened or saved; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what it decodes, but the @b64: reference and the decoded contents become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only values you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @b64: reference provider.
entries.name: b64-ref

entries.description: Status-bar chips for the background self-improvement review and batch context compaction: review running/done/stale with live elapsed time, a turn-countdown fill bar to the next nudge, an always-visible compaction chip (compacting/done/failed/stale with committed reduction or failure class), reply-guard recovery and review-overlap diagnostics, and a Settings page that tunes both orphan ceilings. Disclosure — renderer-only; polls filtered read-only tails of agent.log via host.logs to parse lifecycle markers; listens for review.summary/message.start/message.complete events; stores three small plugin-storage records (settings + last compaction + last review); no network calls beyond the local gateway, no credential access, no self-update.

Native Python plugin, no dependencies. T3 sends then still need a dry-run confirm token and hard guards, but T2 writes (events, purchases, consent, bulk upserts) need no token unless safety.tier2 is token_only; T1 writes (tags, tag/field definitions, drafts, upserts up to bulk_threshold) are never gated and still run under environment=disabled; environment=staging does not block sends, only environment=disabled blocks T2/T3.

entries.description: Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read DUCKWORK_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.

entries.description: Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `duckwork blackbox setup` installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), and joins the DKG peer-to-peer network; package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the Duckwork homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `duckwork blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700.
known_issues: After installing, run `duckwork blackbox setup` once: it installs Blackbox's local DKG node (a pinned, checksum-verified OriginTrail release from npm) and its graph store (Blazegraph in Docker, or Oxigraph when Docker is not available), then syncs the verified threat graph. Until setup has run, the built-in rules protect and `duckwork blackbox status` says setup is needed.
entries.name: blackbox
entries.title: Agent Blackbox

entries.description: Official Blender Lab MCP server over stdio, pinned to upstream v1.0.3, with a Blender workflow skill. Needs Git and uv; Blender 5.1+ is not needed at install. First startup downloads Python dependencies; prepare the uv environment before connecting. Disclosure — tools execute arbitrary Python in Blender with your privileges; the skill starts Blender with online access for that session only (your saved preference is unchanged), and the add-on's local server on port 9876 has no password, so any program on this computer can use it while Blender is open; only after you agree does the skill download Blender from download.blender.org (about 400 MB, about 1.5 GB unpacked), check it against blender.org's sha256 list and install it in your own folder without administrator rights (Linux ~/.local/opt, macOS ~/Applications, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Blender Foundation; never over an existing Blender), and download the v1.0.3 add-on, check its hash and install or enable it; first start downloads the pinned Blender Lab MCP server and its Python dependencies with uv. Server discovery does not prove scene readiness.

entries.description: A live board your agent builds for you: tabs of notes, tables, charts, KPI cards and live Duckwork data, in the dashboard and Duckwork Desktop. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Desktop, and the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. Reads the dashboard's loopback session token from Duckwork internals (web_server._SESSION_TOKEN) and passes it to the sidecar for live usage/sessions/cron widgets; mounts one token-gated static route for approved widget assets. No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

entries.description: Live per-Bot activity timeline for Duckwork Desktop: turns, tool calls (arguments, result, duration), approvals and Group Chat streams, grouped by Bot or by Group Chat, with one-click tracking for new Bots. Disclosure — local only, no network or telemetry; records every Bot profile's turns, assistant replies, tool arguments and results, approval commands and Group Chat streams (redacted with agent.redact, capped per field, 3-day / 20k-row retention) into one SQLite file shared by all profiles under plugin-data/bot-activity; reads each Bot profile's state.db, profile.yaml and config.yaml read-only; Track now / Update runs `duckwork -p <bot> plugins install <same source> --ref <same sha> --enable --yes-deps` (or copies the plugin and runs `plugins enable`) in the Bot profiles you track, never re-enabling one you disabled.

A Bot's first turn in a new Group Chat thread, or a re-titled session, can show its room without a thread label.

entries.description: Tell Cabinet the job you need done and it answers with the smallest setup that does it (one chat, a skill, a routine, a Bot or a crew), shows which answers led there, then helps you act: add one of botcabinet.com's 20 Bots (each with its test record shown) as a Duckwork profile, plan a new Bot line by line, or set up a crew of Bots in a handoff order with blocked Kanban cards. Everything Cabinet makes can be removed again from My Bots, and a Bot that Duckwork's own Bots catalog carries is handed over to it, never duplicated. Disclosure — fetches its Bot catalog from https://botcabinet.com/catalog.json on open and Refresh (data only, 2 MB cap) and, after you confirm, creates Duckwork profiles whose instructions (SOUL.md) come from that catalog; can create and archive Kanban cards for a crew; deletes only profiles it created that you have not changed; reads ~/.duckwork/profiles and hashes profile files to track what it made; calls private Duckwork modules (duckwork_cli.profiles, kanban_db), so a Duckwork update can break it; no shell, credentials, telemetry or self-updates.

Then hire a whole crew in one call, ask what is waiting on you, and edit, teach, share and health-check Bots by chatting. Sends each turn to the user's own brethof-brain memory (on their machine at 127.0.0.1:8610, or hosted at memory.brethof.cloud). Needs a brethof-brain account. entries.description: Run Duckwork' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; Duckwork' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; connections to Browserless carry a browserless-duckwork-plugin/<version> User-Agent so Browserless can count plugin usage (opt-out: BROWSERLESS_SOURCE_TAG=false; the browser's own user agent is unchanged); no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no other telemetry.

entries.description: Bubblewrap terminal backend for Linux: every terminal and execute_code command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's own paths, with a read-only root, a writable working directory (per profile: restricted, workspace or network), the dot entries of the home directory (credential stores always) and the Duckwork home hidden, private temp and process directories, agent and docker sockets masked, and per-command memory, CPU and process limits (`duckwork config set terminal.backend bubblewrap`). Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it runs your commands through the `bwrap` and `prlimit` binaries you install (bubblewrap, util-linux), and under the default `network` profile those commands share the host network. It reads no credentials. File tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) still run on the host and are not confined, and because the working directory is a real host directory Duckwork keeps its dangerous-command prompts, as for the local backend.
entries.name: bubblewrap

entries.description: Bunny Space gateway adapter for Duckwork Agent. Connects a Duckwork profile (the bot brain) to the Bunny Space relay so the bot joins private rooms, answers its owner, and handles @bot:<slug> mentions in posts and comments. Outbound pull transport; no external dependencies. Disclosure — replies are prompted to be in Spanish; @bot mention tasks and assistance tasks are dispatched to Duckwork under the fixed sender id "owner" (BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOWED_USERS must contain "owner"), and the plugin refuses to dispatch third-party content unless platform_toolsets.bunny_space is restricted to read-only tools (the platform's effective toolset, including MCP and plugin toolsets; add no_mcp when MCP servers are enabled); the private assistance worker is opt-in via BUNNY_SPACE_ASSISTANCE=1 (the relay cannot enable it); setting BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS makes the connector refuse to connect; the relay sets the poll interval and may hand the connector a WebSocket "wake" URL it then connects to (wake signals only, no message content).

entries.description: Tells the user when a chat is getting too long and hands them a short opener for a fresh chat; the new chat pulls the earlier context itself via session_search, no handover document. Fill level from real provider token counts, measured against Duckwork' compaction point by default; notices at 70 % and 90 % (configurable), once each per chat, re-armed after compaction, never in cron, subagent, kanban, batch or webhook runs. Notice in the conversation language, English or German. Disclosure — on the turn that crosses a threshold, pre_llm_call adds a one-turn instruction to that turn's user message (never the system prompt; replayed byte-identical, so prompt caching stays intact); post_api_request stores per-session token counts, model and provider name and which notice fired (no message content) under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/chat-length/, pruned after 30 days; reads the session title read-only from state.db and the compression settings read-only from config.yaml; no network calls, no tools, no dependencies.

entries.description: Your house and family chore board as Duckwork tools, through ChorePilot's own MCP server on this machine, the LAN or Tailscale. Runs appliances (lights, climate, dishwasher/washer/dryer, sprinklers, vacuum and more via Home Assistant, Home Connect, MQTT or a simulator) and keeps a rotating chore board that devices verify. ChorePilot's policy decides every call: water/heat actions wait for the person's own yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent's approval queue, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available to an agent. Bundles the chorepilot:household skill. Disclosure — each tool call sends HTTP requests with the bearer token in CHOREPILOT_TOKEN to the user's own ChorePilot server at CHOREPILOT_URL, and the plugin also lists that server's tools once at every Duckwork start (plain http only to loopback, private, Tailscale or .local/.lan/.ts.net addresses); chorepilot_call runs any device or chore tool the token's person may use (lights, climate, vacuum, locking and more) without a Duckwork approval prompt, with ChorePilot's own policy deciding, so water/heat actions wait up to two minutes for that person's yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available; no other network calls, no files read outside the plugin, no background processes, no telemetry, stdlib only.

entries.description: Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for Duckwork — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. Captures every turn durably, extracts beliefs with provenance, answers from memory (raw-tier fallback and abstention), derives scoped conclusions, and compresses the context window losslessly with a restorable record. Registers the memory-provider AND context-engine slots from one shared core, and ships the Tapestry dashboard. Disclosure — off-host embedding endpoints are refused by default (RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT and https peers); sending memory excerpts off the host requires opting in via embeddings.allow_remote. Disclosure — the git mirror (engine/gitmirror.py) is on by default and writes plaintext JSONL copies of memory into a local git repo at ~/.duckwork/commons/db/chronicle/git; it pushes only when git_remote is configured, and its 'encryption' option is a repeating-key XOR obfuscation, not cryptographic encryption.

Registers one web provider, with no new tools, hooks, background processes, file writes, or self-updater. Independent community plugin.

Duckwork' shared search cache omits profiles and routing settings, so repeated queries can reuse another profile's result or an earlier provider, account, gateway, or BYOK route. Settings → Plugins → Codex Theme offers appearance mode, reading width, content spacing, text & code font presets, user/assistant chat bubble colors and a bilingual (EN/中文) UI as native controls; the theme paints theme-level tokens only and never writes user-configurable settings such as --chat-text-scale. v1.2.0 is a compliance release — the composer-drag and input-focus-guard features of the v1.1 line were removed because they patched prototypes and captured global events, which catalog rule 8 forbids.
