entries.description: A live situational-awareness globe in Duckwork Desktop: earthquakes (USGS), disaster alerts (GDACS), natural events (NASA EONET), US severe weather (NWS), military and nearby aircraft (adsb.lol), satellites propagated live from CelesTrak elements, GDELT news incidents, official traffic cameras (Transport for London, Singapore LTA) and shipping chokepoints on a dithered 3D globe, with satellite orbits, aircraft tracks and live camera stills, country dossiers (World Bank facts, events, headlines), NOAA space weather, markets, a feed of events, headlines and alerts, and a passive recon toolkit (DNS, RDAP, TLS, security headers, CT subdomains, CVE with CISA KEV, IP, GitHub, MAC). Five agent tools (osint_situation, osint_events, osint_country, osint_recon, osint_news) answer from the same sources in any chat, and the page's Brief me, Ask Duckwork and dossier buttons open a chat that uses them. No keys needed; an optional TWELVEDATA_API_KEY (plugin setting, read through Duckwork's secret scope) adds equities and commodities. Unofficial; not affiliated with any data provider. Disclosure — the gateway fetches public data from fixed hosts (earthquake.usgs.gov, eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov, gdacs.org, api.weather.gov, data.gdeltproject.org, api.adsb.lol, celestrak.org, services.swpc.noaa.gov, api.tfl.gov.uk and api.data.gov.sg (camera lists), and camera stills from TfL's JamCams bucket on s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com and images.data.gov.sg, fetched only by camera id for a camera the user opens, api.worldbank.org, the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, Guardian and France 24 RSS feeds, api.coingecko.com, and api.twelvedata.com with the key in a header when set), cached and only while the page is open or a tool is called, with a duckwork-osint-map User-Agent; recon sends the domain, IP, CVE id, GitHub name or MAC prefix the user or agent enters to dns.google, rdap.org, crt.sh, cve.circl.lu, cisa.gov, ipwho.is, api.github.com and api.macvendors.com, and the TLS and headers lookups connect directly to the host named, refusing private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and other internal addresses on every redirect, on ports 443/8443 (TLS) and 80/443/8080/8443 (headers) only; GDELT incidents are machine-coded from news coverage and labelled as such; the page keeps its layer choices in Desktop plugin storage; no files written, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.description: Proton Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive for a Duckwork Agent, through an MIT-licensed client built from Proton's own open-source Go libraries (go-srp, go-proton-api) — no Proton Bridge and no paid plan. Reads, searches and sends mail (attachments, scheduled send, labels, folders), manages calendar events and RSVPs, contacts (signed/encrypted vCards), and Drive (upload, download, move, rename, trash, public share links). Sign-in runs in a terminal via `duckwork proton login` and the account password is never taken through chat; sending is refused until a recipient allowlist is set and every send is gated by Duckwork's pre_tool_call approval. Disclosure — talks to Proton's private, undocumented web API over the network; stores a per-account session file (0600) holding OAuth-style tokens and the derived key passphrase (never the password) under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first load copies any sessions from the standalone client's `~/.config/protonlite` into it; reads local files you approve for attachments and Drive uploads and writes downloaded attachments and Drive files under that plugin-data folder; shells out to gpg for calendar/Drive key provisioning; `proton_schedule_followup` creates one-shot Duckwork cron jobs (read-only Proton toolset) that run unattended and deliver to your home channel; no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry.

The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local Duckwork data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (DUCKWORK_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <duckwork_home>/duckwork-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local Duckwork backend.

entries.description: Track subscription quotas and reset times in Duckwork Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the Duckwork Python interpreter located via DUCKWORK_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the Duckwork installer's managed venv (DUCKWORK_HOME/installs). Every credential read is read-only and nothing is refreshed or stored: it reads provider API keys from the process environment, the Duckwork .env, the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source, keyed by a hash of BW_SESSION, which is never sent) and Docker s6 container env files; Duckwork's saved OAuth logins (auth.json credential pool and DUCKWORK_HOME/.anthropic_oauth.json); and other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins: Claude Code (credentials file, macOS keychain or Windows Credential Manager), Codex, Cursor (macOS keychain and the IDE's state.vscdb, opened read-only), Kimi, Grok, ZCode and Command Code. For GitHub Copilot (on by default) it tries COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN (through Duckwork get_secret, else the process environment), then the Copilot editor's apps.json / hosts.json, then runs gh auth token (prompts disabled, 3-second limit), trying each token in turn until GitHub accepts one. It sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint, presenting the vendor client's identity headers where a private endpoint expects them (Claude Code and Codex CLI user agents, the Grok CLI client headers, and for Copilot the VS Code / Copilot Chat editor headers on api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, which GitHub does not document); environment variables such as GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GROK_HOME change which host or file it uses. Usage results are cached under DUCKWORK_HOME/cache/resetwatch, never tokens. It exposes nothing to the model: it is a Desktop page only.
entries.name: hermes-resetwatch

entries.description: Jev-powered Duckwork plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after Duckwork redact_for_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the Duckwork redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive_reasoning_effort false). Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — By default, adaptive effort sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message, and hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters plus skill names, to TypeSafe/OpenRouter Jev after Duckwork redact_for_egress (greetings and light turns stay local). The jev_session_search_rerank and jev_computer_use DOM tools send query/card and public-page text using the plugin's own masking. Off unless enabled: evidence prefetch sends source files the user names under evidence_finder_root (up to 80 KB), cross-tool stuck advice sends redacted error excerpts, and the switchyard-approvals provider, once selected for auxiliary.approval, sends flagged shell commands and your approval policy to OpenRouter Jev, whose confident verdict can auto-approve them (any failure falls back to a human prompt). /switchyard effort receipt saves the plugin's own setting to config.yaml.

entries.description: Give your agent a team: named subagents with their own instructions, tools and model, which it assigns work to, checks on and steers mid-task. The operator defines the roster; the agent follows up with a digest of earlier results and can work a Kanban teammates lane with a review handoff. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock Duckwork; no patched core. Disclosure — adds six tools (teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_check, teammate_wait, teammate_message, teammate_stop) and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process Duckwork subagents using credentials selected by Duckwork from the parent, delegation settings or an operator-configured teammate route where supported. Toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch); Duckwork can add inherited MCP toolsets back unless delegation.inherit_mcp_toolsets is false. A teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where Duckwork provides it, otherwise delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. Optionally the roster is read from an operator-named YAML file (roster_file, relative to the profile home or absolute, so several profiles can share one); the plugin never writes it. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries, role hashes and available token receipts; no full transcripts). It does not read credential stores. Where supported in-process, subagent_start and post_api_request hooks collect token receipts for mapped child sessions. For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. It runs one in-process monitor thread per run to retain finished results and, for lane runs, keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. Completion-notice code exists but never injects on current Duckwork because the host cannot bind notices to the receiving session; use teammate_wait instead. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this repository with gh only after the user approves the draft.
entries.name: hermes-teammates

entries.description:
Security guardrails for Duckwork tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — duckwork-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $DUCKWORK_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.
entries.name: hermes-tenuo

entries.description: Tripo 3D tools on Tripo's v3 API (openapi.tripo3d.ai). Text, photo or multiview to 3D, image edits, retexturing, splitting into parts, Smart UV, auto-rigging, preset animations, retopology, format conversion (FBX, USDZ, STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLTF) and downloads, with an inline 3D viewer in Duckwork Desktop that shows whether a model is really rigged, a library pane that shows where each model came from (the steps behind it, its prompt, a jump back to the chat that made it, and one-click next steps), a local model inspector, and a status-bar chip with the Tripo balance and this chat's spend. Every credit-spending call goes through Duckwork's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a per-chat limit (a setting under Settings → Plugins, default 100 credits) makes it ask again past it. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY. Unofficial; not affiliated with Tripo or VAST. Disclosure — sends prompts and the local images or 3D model files you or the agent name (up to 50 MB; every local-file upload, free calls included, goes through Duckwork's approval prompt) to Tripo's API at openapi.tripo3d.ai with TRIPO_API_KEY; saves downloaded models to $DUCKWORK_HOME/tripo/ or a folder the agent picks (never overwriting: a clash gets a " (2)" suffix), and the Desktop viewer's save button copies models into your Downloads/Tripo folder (or the folder set in its settings); keeps a local task history in $DUCKWORK_HOME/tripo/history.json (chat id, tool, prompt, parent task, estimated cost, saved file paths; at most 2,000 tasks, never sent anywhere); the Desktop library opens local .glb/.fbx/.obj/.stl files only from inside your home folder, $DUCKWORK_HOME/tripo/ or the viewer's download folder, and uploads nothing; the status-bar chip reads your Tripo balance every two minutes and after each Tripo tool call; no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.description: Algorithmic (no-LLM) context compaction engine: builds summaries by deterministic regex extraction instead of a summarizer-model call — zero-token, byte-reproducible, inside the built-in ContextCompressor; compacted turns stay searchable via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, no env vars, no secrets, no telemetry; registers no tools/hooks/middleware and reads only the turns the host passes for compaction; debug: true (default false) writes one metadata-only file $DUCKWORK_HOME/vcc-debug.json. Derived from pi-vcc (MIT, sting8k)
entries.name: hermes-vcc

entries.description: Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your Duckwork session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read_file, search_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in DUCKWORK_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read_file/search_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/duckwork-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the process environment or the host `duckwork` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to Duckwork's stored credentials.
entries.name: hermes-verifier

entries.description: Local video editor for your own footage: 45 FFmpeg tools for the agent (cut, silence removal, 9:16 reframe, captions, music with ducking, loudness, platform export and checks) plus a visual editor in Duckwork Desktop with canvas, any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays and music, scenes and an English/German help. 100% local, no API key. Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Disclosure — the Desktop page starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-run token) that can read and write media and image files anywhere under your home folder (and any VE_EDITOR_ROOTS); preview caches go to the system temp folder. The agent tools run ffmpeg/ffprobe on the input paths the model passes and write media, image or .srt files at the output paths it passes (replacing an existing file only with overwrite: true).
known_issues: Requires FFmpeg and ffprobe on PATH (apt install ffmpeg / brew install ffmpeg / winget install Gyan.FFmpeg).
lk_transcribe_captions is optional and needs 'pip install faster-whisper' plus a model already on disk.

The visual editor has one main video track plus any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays, audio and scenes; these items sit at fixed times and do not move when the main clips are cut (bundle them in a scene to move them together).
The editor preview needs H.264 or VP8 playback in the app's browser engine; editing and export work without it.
entries.name: hermes-video-editor
entries.title: Video Editor (local FFmpeg)

entries.description: Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on Duckwork private vision helpers, so after a Duckwork update it may silently fall back to the normal path.
entries.name: hermes-vision-inline

entries.description: Named network exits for the agent's browser: ask it to browse from another country and it switches, then verifies by reading back the address the far end actually saw, never trusting a label. Any VPN, WireGuard config or proxy works as a local exit; gluetun containers are discovered automatically and one can be brought up on demand. VPN credentials never reach the agent, the chat or the model. Disclosure -- a root-owned helper, installed out of band by the user through a narrow exact-path sudoers rule, is the only thing that reads the credentials and writes them to a root-only file (the agent names a country, never the key), and it pulls the gluetun image pinned by digest; the helper manages gluetun Docker containers, bringing exits up and down; the plugin registers a tool_execution middleware that holds browser_* calls when no verified exit is up (the kill switch, and optional cross-provider failover); it verifies exits by calling public IP-geolocation services (ipinfo, ifconfig.co, ip2location, cloudflare); credential entry is CLI-only, with no model tool for it -- `duckwork vpn provider <name> --set` (interactive) or `--from-ref`, which resolves a WireGuard config from pass/gopass or a host file host-side and never returns it to the model; opening a .onion needs `duckwork vpn allow-onion`, a terminal command a person runs (no model tool) that turns off Duckwork's own internal-address check so onion names resolve and restarts Duckwork, and the plugin never writes that setting itself; the active profile comes from the plugin context (ctx.profile_name), not a private core import.
entries.name: hermes-vpn

entries.description: Live voice calls with Duckwork over WhatsApp, on the linked-device (personal number) setup most Duckwork users already have, with no WhatsApp Business account. Call your bot's number and talk to your Duckwork: the voice uses Duckwork's own persona (a short briefing fetched from Duckwork) and hands real work to Duckwork mid-call. Or let Duckwork call you for things that matter: whatsapp_call_owner rings only the configured owner number (it has no destination parameter) and reports answered, no answer or declined, so the agent can fall back to another channel, including from cron. A short summary of each call arrives in WhatsApp. Speech runs on Gemini Live (gemini-3.8-live by default), reusing the Gemini key Duckwork already has; any Live setup field is configurable, plus a language lock. Setup is a dashboard tab (pairing QR, settings, test call) or an agent runbook skill. Disclosure — runs a separate sidecar process (Rust, built on whatsapp-rust) that the user starts or installs as a systemd/launchd user service; the binary is downloaded from this repo's GitHub release, built and attested by its release workflow, and checked against checksums pinned in the repo (plus the build attestation when the gh CLI is present). The sidecar becomes an extra linked device of the bot's WhatsApp number through an unofficial protocol, stores that session in the plugin's data directory, and answers only the owner's number. During calls it streams audio to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY (read via get_secret), along with the persona briefing, the outgoing call's reason and ask_duckwork results as text. It calls the local api_server with API_SERVER_KEY for ask_duckwork (a full Duckwork turn with the owner's tools), the persona briefing (at startup and after each call) and the post-call summary, a run that may write to Duckwork memory and whose result is sent to the owner on WhatsApp. The dashboard tab's backend saves only this plugin's settings (through duckwork config set), starts and stops pairing, places test calls to the owner, and restarts the sidecar service (systemctl --user or launchctl). No telemetry.
known_issues: Uses an unofficial, reverse-engineered WhatsApp protocol (whatsapp-rust): WhatsApp updates can break calls, and automated use may get the bot number restricted. Use a number you can afford to lose.
Prebuilt sidecar binaries cover Linux amd64/arm64 and macOS arm64; elsewhere it builds from source (Rust 1.94+, cmake, a C compiler).
entries.name: hermes-whatsapp-voice
entries.title: WhatsApp Voice Calls

entries.description: Resolve Duckwork environment variables from the current user's Windows Credential Manager at startup, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.wincred.map, an ENV_VAR -> generic-credential-target mapping (bare names or wincred:// names); each value is read with CredReadW in the current user's vault and handed to the secret-source orchestrator, which applies it with the usual precedence, provenance and conflict rules. Values may be UTF-8 or UTF-16LE (cmdkey and the Credential UI write UTF-16); anything that does not decode to text, or that contains interior NULs, is skipped with a warning instead of being injected as a mangled key. Disclosure - this source reads your Windows Credential Manager: only the generic credentials named in the map, with no enumeration of the vault. Resolved values become environment variables of the Duckwork process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. The package is read-only and stdlib-only (ctypes): it never creates, updates or deletes credentials, writes no files, starts no subprocesses, makes no network calls and does not self-update. Windows only. Credential Manager is user-scoped, so this raises the at-rest bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles; it is not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — when enabled, reads only the Windows Credential Manager generic credentials named in secrets.wincred.map (no vault enumeration) and injects them as environment variables of the Duckwork process and its children, exactly like .env entries; read-only, stdlib ctypes, no subprocesses, no network, no file writes; user-scoped at-rest protection, not a boundary against code already running as the same user.
entries.name: hermes-wincred

entries.description: THEIA — The Human Environment Intelligence Aperture: virtual-desktop capture, fused stage observation, guarded caches, bounded dynamic workflows, and persistent raw-RGB LocateAnything C++/Q5 CUDA grounding.

entries.description: Answer "why did this process die" on Windows: three read-only tools over the Windows Event Log. win_crash_events reads Application Error / Application Hang / Windows Error Reporting / .NET Runtime records for a time window, decodes the exception code (0xC0000005 -> ACCESS_VIOLATION and the other codes a debugger would name), reports the faulting module, its path and the fault offset, and groups repeated crashes by app and signature. Records are classified by provider as well as by event id, so unrelated providers that reuse ids 1000 and 1001 for informational events are not reported as crashes. win_shutdown_events reads the System log for Kernel-Power 41 unexpected restarts, bugchecks decoded to names (0x9F -> DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE, accepting the decimal form some providers emit), EventLog 6008 dirty shutdowns, 1074 operator-initiated restarts with the process and comment, and the 6005/6006/12/13 start and stop markers. win_eventlog_query is the general case: any channel, filtered by event ids, levels, an exact provider name or a payload substring, returning structured records instead of raw XML. Queries read newest-first and stop at the window start or at a 5000-record scan cap; a call returns at most 200 records and marks truncated payload text. Channel names, provider names and numeric filters are validated before anything is interpolated into the query. Disclosure - this plugin reads the local Windows event logs and hands what it finds to the model: application and faulting-module paths, exception codes and offsets, report ids, service names and provider message text, which routinely includes user and machine paths (C:\Users\<name>\...). Treat tool output like any other local diagnostic dump when sharing it. It reads only the channels the current account may read - Security and some operational logs answer with an access-denied error rather than any attempt to obtain elevation - and it never writes to a log, clears one or configures a channel. Stdlib-only (ctypes wevtapi plus xml.etree): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure — reads the local Windows event logs and hands what it finds to the model: application and faulting-module paths, exception codes and offsets, report ids, service names and provider message text, which routinely include user and machine paths (C:\Users\<name>\...); win_eventlog_query reads any channel the account running Duckwork may read, so an unelevated account gets access-denied on Security and some operational logs while an elevated Duckwork can return Security-log records (logon events with account names and source addresses). It never requests elevation, never writes to, clears or configures a log, and has no Python dependencies, child processes, network calls, file writes or self-update. Windows only.
entries.name: hermes-windows-eventlog

entries.description: Windows and WSL triage skills for Duckwork: processes that survive a quit (orphaned stdio MCP trees, lingering python/uv/node children), WSL-to-Windows interop where an argument reaches cmd.exe as shell syntax, config and encoding traps (UTF-8 BOM, legacy console code pages), and long-path or reserved-name errors. One skill plus a copy-paste command reference; the process, argv and job-object failure modes are pinned to reports #131561, #132069 and #61059 and re-verified against current main. Disclosure — instructions only: no tools, hooks, middleware, network calls or credentials, and the destructive diagnostics are marked and gated on asking the user first.
entries.name: hermes-windows-ops

entries.description: Answer "who holds this port" on Windows. win_port_owners reads the TCP and UDP owner tables through iphlpapi (the same rows netstat -ano prints, with the owning PID attached) and resolves each PID to its image name and path, returning one structured record per endpoint. Filters cover one port, several ports, a process substring, the protocol (tcp, udp or both), the TCP state (listen, established, any state name, or all; UDP rows report bound) and IPv6 inclusion, with a record cap and a per-process summary of the rows returned. Built for the failure mode that stalls agents on Windows: a gateway, backend or bridge that cannot bind, where the error names a port but not the process holding it. netstat -ano prints columns, not fields, and its PID still needs a second command (tasklist, or a PowerShell round-trip) to become an image name; this tool is one in-process call instead of a shell parse plus a join, with no child process and no dependency on PowerShell being installed or allowed by execution policy. A protected process whose image cannot be queried keeps its PID and reports a null process name instead of failing the call. Disclosure - the tool reports the local and remote addresses, ports, PIDs and process image paths that netstat -ano and Task Manager already show, and those values reach the model; treat the output like any other local diagnostic listing. Read-only: no socket is opened, bound or connected, the only process access is QueryFullProcessImageName with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION to read an image name, and there is no memory reading, no handle inheritance and no injection. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only.
entries.name: hermes-windows-ports

entries.description: Answer "what is still running, and who started it" on Windows: win_process_table reads the process table (PID, parent PID, image name) and adds each process's image path and creation time, then marks every row with whether its recorded parent is still the process that spawned it. Windows stores a parent PID rather than a handle, so a child that outlived its parent points at a PID that is either unused or reused by a newer process; a parent that started after its child cannot have spawned it, so both cases are reported as gone or reused instead of a plausible but wrong parent name. Filters cover one PID, several PIDs, a name or path substring, a parent PID, and an orphans-only view of what outlived its parent, with a result cap and an option to leave out Windows session processes. Use it for leftover gateway/backend/server children after a quit, for telling thirty python.exe rows apart by start time, and for checking whether a process started before or after the thing being debugged. Read-only: processes are opened with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION for QueryFullProcessImageName and GetProcessTimes only - no memory reads (command lines are deliberately out of scope), no handle duplication, no writes, no child processes. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure - the tool reports image names, image paths and start times to the model, and those routinely include the user and machine name (C:\Users\<name>\...) and reveal which editor, shell or agent started which process; treat the output like a Task Manager screenshot.
entries.name: hermes-windows-process

entries.description: The Duckwork desktop app in your browser. `duckwork workbench` serves the desktop interface through the Duckwork dashboard, for headless servers, VPSes and tablets. Disclosure — community plugin, not a Fordex product. On the first `duckwork workbench` run and again after each Duckwork update it runs `npm install --ignore-scripts` (guided by Duckwork's lockfile) and Vite against your Duckwork checkout's desktop sources, writing only under ~/.duckwork/duckwork-workbench and its own plugin dir (the checkout is only read), and starts `duckwork dashboard` on loopback when none is running.
entries.name: hermes-workbench

entries.description: Kanban board groups and worker health in the Duckwork Desktop footer: blocked cards first and red, live running state as a coloured dot, hover for the breakdown, one click to open the board. Worker-only fork of duckwork-monitor. No credentials are read and there is no network egress; it opens kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only and returns counts only. Zero model tokens.
entries.name: hermes-worker-monitor

entries.description: Agent-owned workflow graphs for Duckwork — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock Duckwork; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop; each agent node is a child duckwork chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside Duckwork' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $DUCKWORK_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through Duckwork' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml and POSTs a wake turn to the local Duckwork API server — the gate.held wake only relays the gate to the human, but the run.done wake tells the woken session to turn the run's findings into tracked work and dispatch follow-up work (as PRs) before the turn ends, and the run.failed wake to apply one corrective amend/repair/resume; a transform_llm_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW_MAX_SEATS (that key only) from $DUCKWORK_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; state lives under $DUCKWORK_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No other network of its own.
entries.name: hermes-workflows

entries.description: Run Duckwork' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and duckwork doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). DUCKWORK_WSL_DISTRO and DUCKWORK_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and Duckwork never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in Duckwork is patched or rebound at runtime.
entries.name: hermes-wsl-terminal

entries.description: Run Duckwork' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.
known_issues: container_disk is reported but not enforced: wslc has no --storage-opt.
No capability dropping: wslc rejects --cap-drop and --security-opt, so dangerous-command approval stays enabled.
entries.name: hermes-wslc-sandbox

entries.description: The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to Duckwork as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal Duckwork turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.
entries.name: hermes-xai

entries.description: Local ledger of the turns in which the agent changed files with write_file or patch: /edit-log shows how many turns changed files, how many files in all, the median per turn, the most changed file type and how long ago the last one was, per model, platform or day, a table of file types (extensions), or the newest turns, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /edit-log recent lists the newest turns (ten, or up to 100 with /edit-log recent 50). A turn another plugin keeps going is counted once. Disclosure — subscribes to pre_verify as an observer only: always returns nothing, so it never keeps the agent going or changes a turn; writes turn metadata (model, platform, file count, files per extension, a 12-digit hash of the session id; never a path, file name or answer text) to plugin-data/edit-ledger/edits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; never opens the changed files; no network
entries.name: edit-ledger

entries.description: Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through Duckwork' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.
entries.name: effortless-hermes
entries.title: effortless-duckwork

entries.description: ElevenLabs sound effects for Duckwork: one tool, elevenlabs_sound_effect, that turns a text description ("glass shattering on a tile floor", "90s hip-hop drum loop, 90 BPM") into an audio file, 0.5 to 30 seconds, optionally a seamless loop, and sends it to you in chat. Bundles a sound-design skill with a local ffmpeg script (trim, loudness, mono, loop fixing, game variation packs) and, in Duckwork Desktop, an inline sound card and a sound library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Duckwork's ElevenLabs voice; a restricted key needs the Sound Effects permission); every call is a paid generation billed to your ElevenLabs account. Only the sound description and its parameters are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set). Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Duckwork home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Duckwork).
entries.name: elevenlabs-sound-effects
entries.title: ElevenLabs Sound Effects

entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI backends for Duckwork' image_generate, video_generate and text_to_speech tools (backend `empiriolabs` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider and tts.provider): image generation and editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-speech, with models and voices from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure: registers three backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool is called, the prompt, source images or text to speak go to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, read through Duckwork' secret scope, and each call is billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account with no Duckwork approval prompt; it reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models), polls GET /v1/jobs/{id} while a generation runs (videos up to 15 minutes by default), downloads the generated files from the returned URLs into Duckwork' cache (the key is never sent to them), and reads a local image file only when the agent asks to edit one.
entries.name: empiriolabs-media
entries.title: EmpirioLabs AI Media

entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI as a Duckwork model provider (provider id `empiriolabs`): chat models with tool calling from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog, each with its context window, image input and reasoning support declared to Duckwork, a low-cost auxiliary model picked from the same catalog, and `reasoning_effort` sent only when you choose a level and the model accepts it. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests (prompts, tool definitions and tool results) go through Duckwork' own client to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, which Duckwork reads, and are billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account; the plugin itself only reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models, kept in memory for an hour), writes no files and starts no processes.
entries.name: empiriolabs
entries.title: EmpirioLabs AI

entries.description: Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for Duckwork Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from duckwork-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from duckwork-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Duckwork task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as Duckwork agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.
known_issues: Codex subscription authentication is managed with `codex login` outside Duckwork; the plugin does not read or write Codex OAuth files.
Full two-sided persistent voice history and a phone voice client are not included in version 0.2.7.
entries.name: enchanted-composer
entries.title: Enchanted Composer

entries.description: Durable local memory for Duckwork agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under DUCKWORK_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to DUCKWORK_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to DUCKWORK_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Duckwork core, and is off by default.
entries.name: entropicmem

entries.description: Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many Duckwork could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors days puts one day on each line, newest first; /errors recent lists the newest failures (ten, or up to 100 with /errors recent 50) and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, Duckwork's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network
entries.name: error-ledger

entries.description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Duckwork model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <DUCKWORK_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "duckwork evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Duckwork shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run duckwork -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "duckwork evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into DUCKWORK_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "duckwork evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query duckwork chat on the routed model (Fordex provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except DUCKWORK_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "duckwork evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under. Disclosure — "duckwork evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <DUCKWORK_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "duckwork evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "duckwork evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.9.2,<0.10), declared as a Python dependency that Duckwork installs on your confirmation.
entries.name: evalroute

entries.description: Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with duckwork tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with duckwork cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run duckwork cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of Duckwork, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.
entries.name: event-read

entries.description: Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

entries.description: Learn Duckwork by doing real work. Four paths (Messenger, Traveler, Crossroads, Boundary Keeper) climb Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced to a capstone on a problem of your own, and a fifth, Guide, covers setting Duckwork up for a client: practice labs built from made-up data, a proposal, one real service run by a scheduled job for several days, a recovery drill, and a review signed by a reviewer you choose. Every mission ends with a check on something you made; your own Duckwork scores your written answers in a new chat; passed missions come back for short spaced reviews; and at the end of a path you can create a Field Record, your own self-issued learning record. Field Academy is an independent community plugin. It is not made, issued or endorsed by Fordex. Disclosure — no network calls (a source link opens in your browser only when you click it); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill: pre_llm_call may add one sentence offering a practice to the user message, only in interactive desktop, TUI and CLI sessions, and post_tool_call records which tool was used; pressing Try it or a scoring button opens a new chat and sends the practice or scoring prompt there (on an older Duckwork it goes to the clipboard instead); the Desktop page calls gateway list methods only (session.list, cron.manage list, skills.manage list, tools.list, mcp.catalog, commands.catalog, setup.runtime_check); stores progress, pasted documents, practice labs, review packets and saved Field Records in $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/; reads a file you name (UTF-8 text, max 5 MiB) and hashes a recording you name without copying it; Guide labs write and check made-up .env and auth.json files inside its own labs folder (refusing to build in a real Duckwork home) and never read Duckwork's real ones; on the Guide path reads Duckwork's run-history database read-only, jobs.json and up to 25 log files (2 MiB each), keeping only timestamps for the job you name, and reads install-stamp.json for the Duckwork version; no private Duckwork imports.
entries.name: field-academy

entries.description: Lifelike voices for your agent: Fish Audio's expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, plus transcription, voice cloning and a voice library. The official Fish Audio plugin: Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Duckwork Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Duckwork speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and live dictation captions on Duckwork 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices and fish_transcribe tools, /fish and duckwork fish commands, and four skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to api.fish.audio's realtime speech-to-text endpoint while you speak, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model (free through 30 November 2026), whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Duckwork stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Duckwork's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and Duckwork config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Duckwork's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Duckwork dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Duckwork's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this plugin's repository as a public GitHub issue or comment with your gh login only after you approve the exact text; reports leave out keys, credit amounts and your own voice ids, and security problems go to the repository's private advisory form instead. No telemetry.
known_issues: Duckwork's text normaliser alters <|speaker:N|> markup and Drama 3 closing tags such as </whisper> on the plain text_to_speech path; use fish_speak for multi-speaker speech and Drama 3 word tags (DuckMind/duckwork#133131).
In the dark theme an empty API key field in Settings is very hard to see; a fix is proposed (DuckMind/duckwork#138994).
Under plugins.isolation: host the duckwork fish terminal command is unavailable and voice replies use whole-file speech instead of streaming; /fish, the tools and both providers still work.
entries.name: fish-audio
entries.title: Fish Audio

entries.description: For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`duckwork fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). Ships two skills (managed-scope admin, recurring tasks). Disclosure — records only model, reasoning effort and service tier per role (no message content, headers or keys) via the pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call hooks and a pass-through llm_execution middleware, stored in $DUCKWORK_HOME/fleet-policy/observed.json; crons --cost opens cron/executions.db and state.db read-only and checks each cron run's final reply locally for silence; watch is an operator CLI command that calls one MCP tool at the config's server_url (or the admin-pinned watch_server_url) with config headers in which ${VAR} env values are expanded, follows redirects, and writes seen ids to a state file at the config-chosen path; the recurring-tasks skill has the agent write watch configs under $DUCKWORK_HOME/watches, a script under $DUCKWORK_HOME/scripts and a cron job; no other network access, no telemetry.

entries.description: Talk to your Duckwork from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a Duckwork pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny), within Duckwork's approval timeout. The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Session hooks feed a dashboard on paired devices with each agent session's platform, a short id and its state (idle, busy, waiting for approval); a device that can switch profiles also sees the offered profiles' sessions. Optional profile switching (off unless `profiles` is set in the default profile's gadget config) lets a device paired on the default profile talk to the listed profiles; each profile approves the device through its own pairing flow (the device shows the `duckwork -p <profile> pairing approve` command), the plugin writes nothing into other profiles, and revoking the device in the default profile sends it back there. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg; Opus reply audio uses the host's libopus when installed (loaded with ctypes, not bundled). `duckwork gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. Writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses Duckwork's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Fordex.
entries.name: gadget
entries.title: Duckwork Gadget

entries.description: In the Godot 4 project open in your editor, it places assets into the scene, plays the game, and the next plan fixes each error from its file and line. Disclosure — Needs Godot 4.7 or later, the Godot AI 4.x add-on, and uv. The first start downloads godot-ai==4.3.0 from pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org. There is no API key. The editor is reached only on 127.0.0.1. A server this plugin starts sends no telemetry. The add-on follows godot_ai/telemetry_enabled (on by default) and can send usage to godot-ai-telemetry-v2-pudmurzsnq-uw.a.run.app. plan_change sends only the session list. apply_plan asks once. A plan that deletes, overwrites, drops unsaved work, writes outside the project or runs code it wrote is not made when what is lost exceeds 1,700 characters, and otherwise runs only after confirm_risky_plan. Play and tests ask once and run the project's code. Tools are on by default on every surface, including the gateway, so anyone who can message Duckwork there can ask and approve. This plugin keeps no user list of its own. Cron, duckwork chat -q and unattended runs decline. Data stays in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-game-editor-<id> after removal. Stop with duckwork plugins disable game-editor, or duckwork tools for one surface. macOS only.
entries.name: game-editor

entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into Duckwork as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.
entries.name: gbrain-plugin

entries.description: Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.
entries.name: gbrain-pointer
entries.title: GBrain Pointer

entries.description: pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `duckwork plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.
entries.name: gbrain-retrieval-reflex

entries.description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Gemini Live API — a status-bar minibar for the Duckwork desktop app (transcript, model catalog, thinking level, session token meter, auto-redial via session resumption). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost and receives single-use ephemeral tokens. No agent tools; desktop-focused, dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory.
entries.name: gemini-live-bridge

entries.description: Google Gemini image (Nano Banana) and video (Gemini Omni) generation backends for image_generate and video_generate, in one plugin built on the google-genai SDK. Image: text-to-image and reference-guided editing (up to 14 images). Video: text-, image- and reference-to-video with native audio. Model picker comes from the key's live models.list. Disclosure — prompts, reference images and the Gemini API key (GEMINI_API_KEY, falling back to GOOGLE_API_KEY, the key Duckwork's own Gemini chat provider uses) are sent to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; reference-image URLs are downloaded by the plugin (public hosts only, redirects re-checked) and a local reference path can be any image file the user can read (accepted only after a magic-byte check); generation is billed to the API key's Google project; writes generated media under $DUCKWORK_HOME/cache/generated/ and a model-list cache (key hash only) under $DUCKWORK_HOME/cache/gemini_media/; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates. Installs google-genai.
known_issues: The Gemini Omni video endpoint stalls intermittently; calls are bounded by a wall-clock deadline (default 300 s) and return error_type timeout.
Video input (editing, extending, reference videos) is not supported; API-key authentication only.
entries.name: gemini-media

entries.description: Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by Duckwork.

entries.description: Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/duckwork-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `duckwork autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `duckwork autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call.
known_issues: One V4A patch that moves a symlink and then updates the moved path can miss the edited file on case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems; commit first or send the Move and the Update as separate calls.
entries.name: git-autosave
entries.title: Git Autosave

entries.description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Duckwork touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.
entries.name: git-hook

entries.description: Git review pane for Duckwork Desktop: every changed file of the agent's last turn, uncommitted, staged or unstaged work, the branch since it left the default branch, or any selection of commits, in one scroll, unified or split, with syntax colours; cites changed lines into the composer as @line: references; and stages, unstages, discards, commits, pushes and opens pull requests from the pane. Disclosure — reads run git subprocesses (rev-parse, status, diff, log, show, cat-file, ls-files, for-each-ref, branch, remote, rev-list, merge-base, symbolic-ref, hash-object) with timeouts and output caps, external diff and textconv drivers disabled. Writes run only when the user clicks: git add, restore, reset, rm, commit and push, on paths validated inside the repository; discard asks first in Desktop's confirmation dialog and deletes only the untracked files it names. By default hooks are skipped and any write that would run a program named by the repository's own config (filter drivers, signing, SSH or credential commands) is refused; the run_repo_programs setting allows them, and the read_only setting hides and refuses every write. Network use: push to the branch's own name on its remote, and the user's own gh or glab CLI for the PR/MR badge and for Create pull request; the plugin itself makes no network requests. Generate commit message sends what the commit will contain and recent commit subjects to the focused chat's model through Duckwork's commit_message one-shot template, only when clicked. It reads files and history inside authorized repositories only (the focused workspace, configured repos/roots and the latest agent selection), this profile's config.yaml, and the cwd column of the sessions table in state.db (read-only); it writes $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/select.sqlite3 (agent selection requests), Desktop plugin storage (display settings, turn baselines) and, through the actions above, the user's repository. While the pane is open it polls the local backend every 3 s (agent selections) and 5 s (live diffs); the status-bar count and the commit box's branch state refresh every 15 s; no background processes, credentials or telemetry.
entries.name: git-review
entries.title: Git Review

entries.description: Multi-repo GitHub issues & PRs in an Orca-style Tasks view for Duckwork Desktop. Disclosure — uses your logged-in `gh` CLI and `git` through Duckwork Desktop's shell bridge, or a GitHub token you paste in the panel (stored unencrypted in Desktop plugin storage, sent only to api.github.com); scans your configured clone folders for GitHub repos and reads skill names under ~/.duckwork; polls the active-session list of every Duckwork profile every 10 seconds for status chips; approve, close, reopen, comment and merge act on GitHub from the panel; creates git worktrees and opens Duckwork sessions seeded with the issue/PR title and body as fenced untrusted text, and without a shell bridge asks the agent to run the worktree git commands.
entries.name: git-tasks

entries.description: GitHub PRs and issues as a right workspace pane in Duckwork Desktop, via the connected gh CLI. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI; the in-pane update pill only runs `duckwork plugins update gitduckwork` (no fetch-and-replace) and currently compares against upstream main rather than the pinned sha.
entries.name: githermes

entries.description: GitHub Copilot model providers for Duckwork: `copilot` (the Copilot API with your Copilot subscription: GPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok models, sign in with `duckwork auth add copilot` or COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN) and `copilot-acp` (drives your installed GitHub Copilot CLI over ACP). Moved out of Duckwork core; profiles that used Copilot get it installed automatically. A Duckwork Labs plugin: built by Fordex, not supported. Disclosure — signs in with GitHub's device-code flow using the Copilot editor OAuth app, exchanges your GitHub token for a short-lived Copilot token at api.github.com and sends your prompts to api.githubcopilot.com (or models.github.ai); it calls GitHub only for profiles that chose Copilot, never runs `gh` or reads other tools' token files, and caches the exchanged token in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/.copilot_jwt.json. copilot-acp runs your local `copilot` CLI.
entries.name: github-copilot

entries.description: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes. Disclosure — authenticates as a GitHub App from GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID and a private key in GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/_FILE (read from the profile env or DUCKWORK_HOME/.env, held in memory only, never written or logged), falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` when no App variables are set, and reports which identity acted in every result.
