entries.description: Your agent follows up on its own: timed check-ins, recurring checks and watchers that wake it in the same chat when something changes. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or Duckwork event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions). A wake is a turn in the same messaging DM that armed it, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Watchers decide without a model call; the agent answers each wake with a structured verdict (notify or stay silent, never a typed sentinel); a no-op governor slows, then pauses pointless wakes and asks once. Every guardrail is a user setting (quiet hours, daily caps, unanswered mute, floors, lifetimes) that the agent works inside and can never widen. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps; HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire, and a wake that could never fire before it expires is refused. It delivers to messaging-gateway DMs only and needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow_gateway_injection: true. Ships the plugin skill `heartbeat2:heartbeat2-report-problem`, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — wakes and watchers run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes and watchers itself unless you set agent_can_create to ask_first or no; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote <url>` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Duckwork blocks from reading; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.
known_issues: A wake turn that fails at the provider shows Duckwork's own failure notice; the plugin cannot suppress it (DuckMind/duckwork#136749). HeartBeat 2.0 backs all wakes off until a model call on the profile succeeds.

notify=false silences the final reply; platforms that show tool progress by default (Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix) still show a progress bubble per wake turn unless display.platforms.

.tool_progress is off (quiet injection requested upstream: DuckMind/duckwork#136825).
Delivers only to messaging-gateway DMs by default (dm_only); CLI, TUI, Desktop, API-server and cron arming are refused until Duckwork core supports silent injected turns there.
When Duckwork falls back to another model during a wake turn, its model-fallback notice is posted to the chat, even for a wake that stays silent (DuckMind/duckwork#137738).

entries.description: Shared fleet memory for Duckwork agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.

entries.description: Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless an optional online feature is switched on: search by meaning (embeddings: on) or rescoring by a cross-encoder (rerank: on), both off by default. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.duckwork-memory-store) and memory_store.db, so `duckwork update` moves existing users onto it; the schema change is additive and older versions keep working on the file. Taken over from Fordex's handoff copy (Fordex/duckwork-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, duckwork_home, mirror metadata, backup_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as_of a date) and `forget` erases a fact with all its versions from the file; since 0.16.0 a name guessed from a fact's text must be shaped like one and stays provisional until a second fact or a person confirms it, and entities can be renamed or deleted (the facts stay). Since 0.18.0 an optional, experimental second stage reorders the recall candidates with a cross-encoder at a /v1/rerank endpoint that answers in Cohere's shape without a key, such as llama-server (rerank: on, off by default). It does not raise hits: on the maintainer's held-out set (126 questions) it cut non-target facts in the top five by about 40 % and lines per turn by about a third, and lost about one target per hundred questions. Disclosure — local only unless an optional online feature (search by meaning or rescoring) is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($DUCKWORK_HOME/memory_store.db unless db_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; delete_entity removes a name, its aliases and links from the entity index (never a fact) and keeps an HMAC of each name the same way (not of an alias only a fact's text gave, which goes without one), and both rewrite the file so freed pages keep no copy; the first writable open after an upgrade that changes the extraction rules relinks the facts to their entities under the new rules (stores up to 2,000 facts and 500,000 characters; larger ones on fact_store rebuild_entities), changing only the names it guessed and their links, never a fact, a declared name or an alias someone gave; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact_store / fact_feedback calls do unless cron_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry (at the debug log level the recall stages log fact ids and scores, never text), and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on or rerank: on (both off by default). With embeddings: on, the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; with rerank: on, before a turn the user's message and up to rerank_top_k (40) candidate fact texts, and for a fact_store search its query and results, go to the rerank endpoint the user configures (rerank_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name), with no credentials and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject or that look like they hold a secret, and queries that hold one, are not sent; a failure or a slow answer gives the recall of rerank: off and pauses the endpoint (60 s, doubling to 900 s); nothing the endpoint returns is stored; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored.
known_issues: Word forms are matched by stems, not a dictionary: an irregular form can miss (ponies / pony). A synonym is found only if the fact's keywords name it, unless the optional online search by meaning is on; facts stored without keywords (older ones, auto_extract) need `enrich`.

Arabic, Indic scripts, Indonesian, German, Turkish, Polish and Dutch are matched by scanning the facts' text: the first such search after start analyses every fact (about 1-1.5 s at 5,000 facts, 4-6 s at 20,000); stores without such facts never scan. The bundled dictionaries load on the first word of their language (Chinese about 0.2 s and 30 MB).

forget cleans the database file only: Duckwork session history, `duckwork backup` archives and copies other tools made are not rewritten (tools can read the `forgotten` table and clean their own copies by fact id).

rerank: on is experimental and does not raise hits. On the maintainer's held-out set it lost one target in 126 questions with embeddings off and two with them on, on questions where several facts of one kind compete, against about 40 % fewer non-target facts. Each turn waits for one rerank call: on 4 CPU threads about 120 ms median with jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual and 340 ms with bge-reranker-v2-m3, capped by rerank_timeout (3 s, lower with embeddings on so that both fit the core's 8 s prefetch budget). The suggested CPU model, jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual, is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial use only); bge-reranker-v2-m3 is Apache-2.0. The plugin ships no model. It sends no key, so a cloud rerank API that requires one (Cohere, Jina) refuses every call; it is tested with llama-server.

entries.description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.9.11, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; Duckwork does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar/huddo_rename run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, and, if Duckwork can schedule recurring tasks, to schedule one that does the same between turns, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; the server also tells the agent to read the remote guide at https://huddo.ai/SKILL.md before starting (vendor-hosted, not pinned), and the skills point to npx -y huddoai@latest (unpinned) for identity export and app publishing; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) and a local copy of your rooms' messages (used by huddo_search/huddo_show/huddo_files; huddo_sync fetches older history from api.huddo.ai) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skills tell the agent to get confirmation in your own Duckwork chat before anything sensitive.
entries.name: huddo

entries.description: Markdown wiki as Duckwork long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside DUCKWORK_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Duckwork's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at DUCKWORK_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in DUCKWORK_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to duckwork backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

entries.description: HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `duckwork hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `duckwork memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in Duckwork's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through Duckwork's get_secret and reads no Duckwork credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as Duckwork auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `duckwork memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill a free Fordex Portal endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. A server the plugin starts gets that key in its environment; for a server started another way (the launcher, a service) that reports "awaiting_key", the plugin (at most every 10 minutes) and `duckwork hyatlas doctor` POST the key over plain HTTP to /api/v1/llm/key, only when the configured server host is this machine; the server accepts it only from a loopback address and keeps it in memory only, never on disk. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions, recent summaries and newest facts to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY), and, after a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP; off disables it), up to 40 of that stretch's facts to write one episode summary. HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write that sends the new facts together with similar stored ones (including those under user IDs grouped with the owner by HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES) so the model can update, replace or link them; it is meant for a local model. An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. Turns written while the endpoint was unreachable or before a key arrived are extracted later by a catch-up pass (every 10 minutes by default, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_EVERY; rows up to 7 days old, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_MAX_AGE), sending the same text a write would have sent. `duckwork hyatlas doctor` sends one short test prompt ("Reply with the single word OK.") to the endpoint and writes, finds and deletes one test memory. When you replace or remove an entry with Duckwork's memory tool, the plugin asks the local server to retire the matching memory (reversible); nothing leaves the machine. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, Duckwork starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `duckwork hyatlas start` keeps running after Duckwork exits until `duckwork hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `duckwork hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads no credentials (since 4.8.0 it no longer reads Duckwork auth.json). No telemetry.
known_issues: After enabling, select the provider with `duckwork memory setup` (memory.provider: hyatlas) — installing and enabling alone does not activate memory.
The agent tools and hooks arrive through the MemoryProvider interface, not ctx.register_tool, so they do not appear in the plugin tool list.
Requires the separate hyatlas-go server binary (installed by the user); without a reachable server the provider reports unavailable and memory features degrade rather than fail.

Updating the plugin does not update the server: install hyatlas-go v5.0.0 too. A store written by an earlier version can be cleaned with the server's maintenance endpoints (see after-install.md, 'Upgrading a store written before 4.5.0').
5.0 removed share_llm_key: the plugin no longer uses Duckwork's Fordex sign-in. Set your own extraction key (llm_key) with `duckwork memory setup`; `duckwork hyatlas doctor` checks it.

entries.description:
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `duckwork index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the Duckwork env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Duckwork model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $DUCKWORK_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Duckwork env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Duckwork sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.
entries.name: index-network
entries.title: Index

entries.description: Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway can search with your key and approve a watch. Turn a surface off with duckwork tools. index_watch schedule creates one cron job that runs a model turn every 15 minutes (two or more model requests when it calls the tool) with no daily cap, and it watches only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run duckwork cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Scheduling and unscheduling ask for Duckwork approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, where the watch only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The watch relies on private parts of Duckwork, so an update can stop it.
entries.name: index-search

entries.description: Local ledger of the messages models write in the middle of a turn, before their final answer (the text that comes with a tool call, which on chat platforms can arrive as messages of their own): /interim-log shows how many each model wrote, in how many turns, how many per such turn, their median length and how long ago the last one was, per model, provider, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /interim-log recent lists the newest messages (ten, or up to 100 with /interim-log recent 50). entries.description: Signed, independently checkable receipts for Duckwork approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Duckwork passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.
entries.name: invinoveritas-receipts

entries.description: Fleet control for Duckwork Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the local node-cli (`server health`) — the plugin itself makes no raw HTTP calls to the relay; node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files. Tracked task ids are stored in your Duckwork home under plugin-data/iowap/.

entries.description: Rule-based proofreading for Japanese business text: finds and fixes AI-style phrasing (stock phrases, monotonous sentence endings, overused symbols and Markdown, English-calque grammar) with line, column and a fix hint. It checks wording, not authorship, and rarely flags plain model output. A transform_llm_output hook checks every final Japanese answer and only reports by default; opt-in enforce mode rewrites flagged answers with the user's own model and delivers the rewrite only if numbers, names, URLs, code and negation survive and the score drops under the threshold. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; enforce mode sends each flagged answer to the user's configured model (one extra call, a second only when the first rewrite fails the checks or stays over the threshold; extra cost and up to 25 s delay); a read-only post_tool_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; reports stay in process memory on local surfaces only. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; reads plugins.hook_callback_timeout via a private read-only Duckwork helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.
entries.name: ja-writing-guard

Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, and records bounded structured audit logs. entries.name: jev-approvals

entries.description: Skip agent cron runs that would do nothing: a pre-run wake-gate script asks TypeSafe Jev one yes/no question over a small state snapshot (files, changed-since-last-run, localhost URLs) and prints {"wakeAgent": false} when it is confident the run is pointless. Fail-open on every error, forced wake after N consecutive skips, stdlib only. Disclosure — each gated cron tick (and the tool's test action) sends the configured snapshot of file contents, localhost URL response bodies and change flags (≤6,000 chars) to api.typesafe.ai with your TypeSafe key.
entries.name: jev-cron-gate

entries.description: TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for Duckwork' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while Duckwork retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.
entries.name: jev-curator

entries.description: Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing Ollama:Cloud provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. Every other catalog router picks a model and stops, and the two entries that touch reasoning effort move it by hand; this one decides both per turn. Ollama:Cloud only — no other provider is routed, and every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to OpenRouter's Decisions API (typesafe/jev, billed to your OpenRouter key) on every routed turn.
entries.name: jev-effort-router

entries.description: TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.
entries.name: jev-judge

entries.description: Splits one Japanese address into prefecture, city, town and the remainder with address_split, built on Geolonia's address data (CC BY 4.0, from the Digital Agency address base registry). Give it a Japanese postal address as written, such as 東京都千代田区霞が関2-1-2, and it returns the prefecture, city and town as separate fields. Disclosure — Each call sends at most two HTTPS GET requests, with no API key, to japanese-addresses-v2.geoloniamaps.com or the JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL you set (plain http only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost). The matched prefecture and municipality names go into the URL path; the house number, the lot and the building name are not sent. JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL is read for the active profile on each call, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The tool is on for every surface, including gateways, and asks for no approval: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway can call it. Turn a surface off with duckwork tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. It writes no files and creates no cron job. A point can be coarser than the town and is not a rooftop geocode, and an address it cannot place for certain comes back as ambiguous or at the municipality instead of a guess. The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Called from Duckwork with five models in a small sample of 18 sessions (see CHANGELOG.md).
entries.name: jp-address

entries.description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure: no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the Duckwork home); writes PNGs to the Duckwork image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default).
entries.name: jp-charts

entries.description: Talk to Duckwork from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put Duckwork in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use Duckwork commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with Duckwork commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.
entries.name: jp-chatwork

entries.description: Japanese corporate lookup (法人照会): find or verify a company by name or corporate number and read its gBizINFO record (basic info, subsidies, government contracts, awards, certifications, financials, patents, workplace data). Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN in a request header; no other host, nothing written to disk.
entries.name: jp-corporate

entries.description: Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. It finds a Japanese company's annual securities report (yuho) and other financial reports filed on EDINET, and reads headline figures such as revenue and total assets from a filing. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. Each call reads EDINET_API_KEY for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with duckwork tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in Duckwork. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false only means the figure is missing from the consolidated current-year rows the plugin reads, not that the document has no number. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <DUCKWORK_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on Duckwork internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup.
entries.name: jp-edinet

entries.description: Japanese laws for Duckwork Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Ask for one Japanese law article, such as Article 32 of the Labor Standards Act, and it returns the official law text with the law number and the date that version took effect. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, Duckwork tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until duckwork cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; duckwork tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint.
entries.name: jp-egov-law

entries.description: Japanese government statistics from the e-Stat API: search tables and fetch figures such as population, households, wages, and prices, with estat_search_tables, estat_table_info, and estat_get_data. Disclosure — It needs a free e-Stat application ID, set as ESTAT_APP_ID in the .env of each profile. Each call sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp and puts ESTAT_APP_ID in the request URL. The ID is read for the active profile on each call. An HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used, and no other host is called. Nothing is written to disk, and this plugin creates no cron job. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow there can call them with your ID. Turn a surface off with duckwork tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.
entries.name: jp-estat

entries.description: Lists Diet meetings and returns a short speech excerpt, with kokkai_search, kokkai_speech, and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key. kokkai_search returns meeting metadata and the official meeting URL, and does not return speech text. kokkai_speech reads /api/speech and returns at most 10 excerpts, each at most 240 characters, with the speaker, the meeting name, the date, and the speech URL. Those excerpts are not written to plugin-data. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, read a speech excerpt, add a watch, and approve it. Turn a surface off with duckwork tools. kokkai_watch add creates one cron job that runs a model turn once a day, at the hour you pick in Duckwork's own timezone, with no daily cap. It stays after uninstall until you run duckwork cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch asks for Duckwork approval every time and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions, and plugins.isolation: host. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot save seen speech IDs and says so on every run. The watch relies on private parts of Duckwork, so an update can stop it. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs, and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall.
entries.name: jp-kokkai

entries.description: Quarterly MLIT prices for one city, via reinfolib_quarter. Use it for Japanese real estate and property prices in one city: it returns the number of recorded sales, the median trade price and the first 20 rows for a quarter. These are transaction prices, not the official land prices published as 地価公示. Disclosure — sends your REINFOLIB_API_KEY as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key to www.reinfolib.mlit.go.jp (HTTPS, XIT001) or the host of REINFOLIB_BASE_URL. Plain http is refused except 127.0.0.1 and localhost, where the key is not encrypted. On for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow can call it with your key, with no approval prompt, including unattended cron, yolo, and approvals off. duckwork tools does not stop /jp-reinfolib. Stop the slash command with allow_admin_from, user_allowed_commands, group_user_allowed_commands, or by disabling the plugin. After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until duckwork cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register_automation_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be [SILENT] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」
entries.name: jp-reinfolib

entries.description: Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with duckwork tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. The /subsidies command is outside duckwork tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run duckwork cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows.
entries.name: jp-subsidies

entries.name: junie-acp

entries.description: @jwt: context references that decode a JSON Web Token for the model: @jwt:<token> (or a quoted "Bearer <token>") attaches the header with the algorithm in words, every claim as JSON, the exp, nbf, iat and auth_time claims in UTC with how long ago or ahead they are, whether the token has expired and its lifetime, and notes on alg none, a missing or empty signature, a header that names its own key (jku, x5u, jwk), crit and duplicate names; encrypted tokens (JWE) show their header only; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a token as you type it. The signature is never verified. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's base64, json and datetime; no network (no key sets fetched), no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the token, but the @jwt: reference and the decoded header and claims become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only tokens you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @jwt: reference provider.
entries.name: jwt-ref

entries.description: One board, three views, and each answers a different question: List says what the work is, Timeline says when it happened, Graph says what hangs off what. The Graph view draws a card per task and an arrow per dependency, laid out top-down by longest path (or left to right, by status, or as a compact grid), with a transitive reduction that counts the arrows it implies instead of hiding them, links you draw, move and delete where they are drawn, and a click that lights the whole upstream and downstream lineage of a task. The Timeline renders any board as real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a period selector from 6 hours to 7 days. The List view trades the bars for a dense table — task, assignee, status, last activity. Quick scopes (Running, Blocked, Open, All) narrow the board in all three views alike, and a lineage switch widens any of them to what leads to the selection and what follows it. Tasks are created from the page (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parented by drag & drop or from the drawer, and moved between boards with their children; any task with files carries a paperclip, its files listed on demand — the board payload carries only a count — and previewed by type (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or downloaded. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network.
entries.name: kanban-gantt

entries.description: Live, read-only dependency graph of the Duckwork kanban boards in Duckwork Desktop: every board as a band, tasks as cards, dependencies as arrows with implied ones folded away. Click a task to light up its whole lineage with runs, last failure and the running worker's latest tool calls; deep links open a task directly, and a stdlib CLI renders the same graph as a standalone HTML file. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — reads every kanban board database and, for running tasks, the assignee profile's state.db (the kanban worker session's latest assistant messages and tool-call arguments), read-only, and shows them in Desktop through its own local dashboard routes.
entries.name: kanban-graph

entries.description: Live, now-centered Gantt timeline for the Duckwork kanban boards — a slidable, persisted 72 h window (default now -24h -> now +48h; drag to move, drag the ends to resize), free wheel zoom down to hour ticks, a now line, status filtering, an optional done lane, and lifecycle rendering (dashed waiting vs solid run spans at real durations). Fork of kanban-gantt (GPL-3.0). Disclosure — the backend can transition, reassign, comment on and permanently delete kanban tasks on any board (Desktop asks for confirmation before deletes); local SQLite only, no network.
entries.name: kanban-live-gantt

entries.description: Live-stream Duckwork kanban worker activity to a Telegram ops channel: one edit-in-place message per task with rolling tool-call history, elapsed timer, tokens/sec, thinking indicator, and a pinned final state (done/blocked). Mid-task steering via task comments — /steer from Telegram through the bundled companion daemon, or straight from the board. Ships disabled by default; needs a dedicated ops bot (KANBAN_STREAM_BOT_TOKEN + KANBAN_STREAM_ALLOWED_USERS). Outbound calls go only to api.telegram.org; reads the kanban DB read-only; no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — sends kanban task titles, summaries and tool names with command/path snippets to the Telegram chat you configure via your own bot; the optional steer daemon posts allowlisted Telegram users' /steer text as task comments that reach the running worker.
entries.name: kanban-stream
entries.title: Kanban Stream

entries.description: Give every Duckwork kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).
entries.name: kanban-task-threads

entries.description: Web search and page fetching through Keenable's hosted MCP server, with search and research skills: single-site and publish-date filters, result and snippet limits, and page fetches that return only what a prompt asks for. Works without an API key; an optional KEENABLE_API_KEY lifts the keyless rate limits. Adds direct MCP tools beside Duckwork's built-in Keenable web backend and leaves web_search / web_extract provider selection unchanged. Disclosure: connects to Keenable's hosted MCP server at `api.keenable.ai` and sends it the search queries, URLs and fetch prompts the agent issues, labelled with the header `X-Keenable-Title: duckwork-plugin`; sends `X-API-Key` only when the user adds the optional config.yaml entry with their key.
entries.name: keenable-plugin
entries.title: Keenable

entries.description: Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Fordex are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Fordex only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.duckwork/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Fordex it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Fordex inference API with FORDEX_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.duckwork/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.
entries.name: kfchow-llm-value-router

entries.description: The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Duckwork model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Duckwork's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Duckwork cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Duckwork.
entries.name: kimchi-acp-provider

entries.description: Kimchi (kimchi.dev) models via the OpenAI-compatible API — live catalog from the metadata endpoint, API-key auth, gateway unknown-model 400s classified as model_not_found, and an identifying User-Agent (duckwork-agent/<version>) on every gateway request.

entries.description: Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments.
entries.name: kiwi

entries.description: Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume and cancel ask for Duckwork approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway can request a move and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. vision_check, off by default, sends webcam stills to your model. The plugin host cannot watch. Not tested on real hardware.
entries.name: klipper-print-watch

entries.description: Local Kokoro-82M text-to-speech on Apple Silicon: adds the kokoro-mlx speech provider (tts.provider: kokoro-mlx) with sentence-by-sentence PCM streaming for voice mode, read-aloud and text_to_speech, 54 voices in nine languages, an optional voice per language that switches per sentence between Portuguese and English, and an optional dictionary of English words a non-English voice pronounces in English without changing voice; plus duckwork kokoro install, status, restart, voices, say, words and uninstall. Disclosure — duckwork kokoro install creates a separate Python 3.11 environment with uv (about 1.1 GB from PyPI, plus spaCy's en_core_web_sm wheel from its GitHub release, pinned by SHA-256), downloads mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16 at a pinned revision from Hugging Face (about 340 MB), and installs a launchd agent (dev.duckwork.kokoro-tts) that keeps a local server running in the background. The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (it refuses other addresses), runs offline, and does not log the text; the text to speak goes only to that local server, bypassing any proxy settings. Writes the environment, model cache and log under ~/Library/Application Support/duckwork-kokoro-tts, the requested audio files, and the profile's config.yaml only when you run duckwork kokoro words add or remove. No API keys, no telemetry.
known_issues: macOS on Apple Silicon only (MLX).
Under plugins.isolation: host the duckwork kokoro terminal command is not available (Duckwork skips plugin CLI commands in the host); the speech provider still registers.
Only Brazilian Portuguese and English are tested; Japanese and Mandarin may need extra G2P packages this release does not install. Per-sentence language detection covers Portuguese and English.
entries.name: kokoro-tts
entries.title: Kokoro TTS (local, Apple Silicon)

entries.description: Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

Disclosure — connects to Kumiho's hosted MCP at https://mcp.kumiho.cloud/mcp (OAuth at control.kumiho.cloud, tokens held by Duckwork); memory queries, including an automatic topic lookup near the start of relevant conversations, and approved captures are sent there; the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, so Duckwork asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The optional backfill helper reads only files the user names and writes review packets to a new folder; Dream State can create a recurring Duckwork cron task when asked (read-only by default). No local server, telemetry or background process.

entries.description: Langfuse observability for Duckwork: one trace per turn, one generation per LLM call (usage and cost from Duckwork' own pricing, cache and reasoning tokens included), one observation per tool call and subagent. Content capture is sanitized by default (metadata-only and full are opt-in); sends traces only to the Langfuse project whose keys you set. Formerly built into Duckwork core as observability/langfuse; existing users are migrated automatically.

entries.description: Spend USDC in the real world from Duckwork: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the Duckwork approval gate first. entries.description: An Obsidian-compatible map of how your codebase works (modules, flows, integrations, platform traps, decisions), kept outside the repo and kept honest by hooks: a primer on the first turn, pointers to the notes that own what you are asking about or editing, and a reminder through the verify gate when code moved but the map did not. Eight lightkeeper:* skills carry the procedures (init, seed, tidy, trace, release, knowledge-vault, vault-sync, vault-tidy); the vault CLI (find, check, sync, status, log, export) works from any shell. Not a memory provider. Disclosure — each hook runs python3 on the plugin's own scripts as a synchronous subprocess with a 10 s timeout (on every user message, after every write_file and patch, at the verify step and at session end), and those scripts run read-only git commands (rev-parse, remote get-url, worktree list, ls-tree, status, log) in the session's checkout and in the vault folder; the session primer and prompt hints put text from the vault's notes into the model's context; the hooks read the vault registry ~/.claude/vaults and the vault folders it lists, and write only inside the vault (_meta/index.json), a small per-session state file in the system temporary directory ($TMPDIR), and the plugin's own data directory; the init, seed, sync, tidy, trace and release procedures run the vault CLI through the terminal and commit to the vault's own git repository, and vault init appends the vault to ~/.claude/vaults and, only when you pass its opt-in flags, copies a vault launcher to ~/.local/bin (--install-cli), installs report-only post-merge and pre-push hooks in your code checkouts (--git-hook), or adds a post-commit hook that pushes every vault commit to the remote you name (--backup-remote); vault export writes an HTML map that loads d3 7.9.0 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com when opened; no other network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no dependencies beyond Python 3.9 and git. Silent until a vault covers the session's working directory.
known_issues: Verified with a real model on Duckwork stable 0.22.2 in duckwork chat -q mode: patch and write_file, the edit pointer, the verify-gate reminder, the note update and the session-end notice. Not yet verified: the messaging gateways, interactive multi-turn sessions, turns after a context compaction, concurrent sessions on one gateway, and host-unified main builds.

Does nothing until a vault covers the session's working directory: create one with python3 ~/.duckwork/plugins/lightkeeper/bin/vault init <vault folder> --name <name> --repo <checkout> (README, Duckwork Agent section). Needs the local terminal backend.

entries.description:
Local long-term memory for Duckwork agents. Everything stays on your machine: an SQLite store plus bundled embedding and NLI models, no telemetry, no LLMs.
Limbic is designed on the physiological brain, opaque and organic. Memories strengthen or atrophy with use, corrections replace what they superseded — all deterministic background mechanisms, zero LLM calls.
Algorithmic forgetting keeps atrophied memories out of the database. Recall is calibrated: when nothing in memory is confident enough, it abstains instead of guessing, so the agent answers honestly rather than surfacing near-misses. First start downloads ~1 GB of pinned models once, then runs fully offline. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license). Disclosure — the agent-facing tools are remember, recall and forget (forget lists candidate facts for a query, then deletes the one fact id the user picks, scoped to the current user, and appends a hash-only receipt of the content's sha256, length, user id and fact id to limbic.db.deletions.jsonl beside the database); on first primary session start downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB, on first contradiction check) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside DUCKWORK_HOME; %USERPROFILE%\.cache\limbic on Windows); at every model load, every file in those cache folders that is not in the pinned manifest is deleted — including unrelated files if you point embedding/nli cache_dir at a shared folder; spaCy NER models are optional: `duckwork limbic languages --set <lang>` and `duckwork limbic setup` run `python -m spacy download <model>`, which pip-installs each model package (~14.5MB, version picked by spaCy, not hash-pinned) from spaCy's GitHub releases into Duckwork's own Python environment, and `duckwork limbic setup` also pre-downloads both ONNX models; memory stays local in limbic.db under DUCKWORK_HOME, facts whose trust decays to zero are deleted automatically, and duckwork backup adds VACUUM snapshots under DUCKWORK_HOME/backups; no telemetry.

entries.description: Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Duckwork Agent. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY.

entries.description: Memoria Cloud memory provider with scoped recall, explicit memory tools and opt-in background capture. Disclosure — sends recall queries and explicit memory operations to api.thememoria.ai by default (or a configured self-hosted origin). When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active Duckwork profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret.
known_issues: Development preview: local CLI acceptance passed; Desktop has not been validated and gateway platforms are disabled.
Auto capture is off by default. One-shot CLI exit can interrupt an in-flight capture, leaving an uncertain event requiring manual inspection.

Explicit-write exclusions apply to the current turn only. Auto capture can retain paraphrases, recalled facts from later turns, transient results or operation requests; global semantic deduplication is not guaranteed.
Ambiguous write outcomes are not automatically retried; this plugin does not provide exactly-once capture.

entries.description: Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `duckwork memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.
entries.name: memory-rewind

entries.description: Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Duckwork' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Duckwork' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is Duckwork' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Duckwork' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.
known_issues: Needs plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under plugins.isolation: host the plugin cannot see the current chat, sender or Duckwork' review marker, so it judges every call like a direct chat and the group chat and background review protection does not apply.
Covers Duckwork' built-in memory tool (USER.md, MEMORY.md) only, not the tools of memory provider plugins such as Honcho or Mem0.

Without trusted_users every direct chat counts as the owner: whoever can message the agent directly may add facts to the owner profile and correct them (not delete them) until the owner's id is listed.
Spotting USER.md and MEMORY.md edits made through terminal and execute_code is best effort: a path built some other way, or a command run from a script file, can get through.

terminal and execute_code calls are read up to 16,384 characters. A longer call that contains the word memories, USER.md or MEMORY.md (any case, quotes ignored) is refused even when it only reads them; a longer call that contains none of them passes without being read.
entries.name: memory-shield
entries.title: Memory Shield

entries.description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Requires Mixar 4.2.1+ on macOS, Windows or Linux, signed in with Connect MCP turned on, on the same computer as Duckwork. entries.description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms (beta) let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the two bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; Duckwork runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context.
