entries.description: Review boards for UI mockups. The agent builds a board from a decisions.json file and your prototype pages; you open it on desktop or phone, mark each decision approve, change or skip, pin comments on the mocks and press Send, and your agent wakes up with the feedback as a markdown digest. Four mock_review tools, the `duckwork mockreview` CLI and slash command, and a bundled usage skill. Boards are served from your computer (loopback by default, or your tailnet) or published on here.now. Disclosure — when autostart is on (off until `duckwork mockreview setup`), a board web server (127.0.0.1:8790 by default) and one worker thread run inside the gateway process; setting host to 0.0.0.0 exposes every review to your network with no login. Outbound calls: a signed POST to the local Duckwork webhook (localhost:8644) on Send, and, only for reviews hosted on here.now, https://here.now/api/v1 with your HERENOW_API_KEY. Secrets are read through Duckwork's secret scope only. Runs `bash publish.sh` from the official here-now skill (key in the child environment), `tailscale status --json` and `tailscale serve status --json` (read only; on macOS the Tailscale app's own binary if the symlink crashes) for tailnet hosting, and from `setup` the duckwork subcommands `--version`, `gateway status`, `config get/set/unset`, `webhook subscribe`, `webhook remove` (only for a stale self-delivering route, after you confirm) and `plugins validate`. Reviews are stored under $DUCKWORK_HOME/workspace/mock-reviews. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies.
known_issues: here.now hosting needs the official here-now skill in the active profile (`duckwork skills install official/productivity/here-now`) and a HERENOW_API_KEY; local and tailnet hosting need neither.
Waking the agent on Send needs the gateway's webhook platform; `duckwork mockreview setup` enables it and creates the route.
entries.name: mock-review
entries.title: Mock Review

entries.description: Scheduled check that the model you use in Duckwork has not quietly got worse: 34 fixed, exactly graded questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own) run through Duckwork cron, each run tested against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run, and a message only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model or a failed measurement. Not yet tried against a real LLM API (checked with a local mock model and real Duckwork cron). Disclosure — each check calls your own model through ctx.llm on your bill, capped per check by the plugin (default 120,000 tokens / $0.50, no daily cap; the agent can start checks itself via the model_drift tool, and the scheduled agent turn is extra); price lookup goes through Duckwork's pricing code (may fetch OpenRouter/models.dev prices); 10 optional code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child process (not a hostile-code sandbox) including in unattended cron runs when enabled; `schedule` creates one Duckwork cron job that survives plugin removal (run `unschedule` first); writes run history to plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry.
entries.name: model-drift-watch

entries.description: Model leaderboard for Duckwork Desktop: a full /model-leaderboard page that ranks any OpenRouter model for a chosen Duckwork profile — context window, prices, Artificial Analysis indices and curated SWE-bench Verified / LiveCodeBench — with per-profile criteria, six score views (cards, table, score bars, histograms, heatmap, quality-vs-cost Pareto frontier), an OpenRouter news feed (new models, price changes, promos) and a documented REST surface under /api/plugins/model-leaderboard/. Disclosure — outbound HTTPS to OpenRouter's public model API (catalogue and pricing) on a 60 s poll and a forced refresh every 10 minutes while the page is visible, and to Hugging Face's public model API (safetensors metadata, for parameter counts) on demand and cached; reads the installed Duckwork profiles' own config.yaml files once, to seed the tracked list from the models those profiles declare; keeps its state in <duckwork home>/plugin-data/model-leaderboard/ (seeded from the JSON shipped with the plugin), which LLM_DASH_DATA / LLM_DASH_CACHE_TTL can move or tune; the optional "Auto-fill criteria" action runs on the host LLM facade (ctx.llm.complete_structured), so it spends the user's configured model tokens; ships one read-only skill (model-leaderboard:refresh-benchmarks) whose only write is a POST to its own /benchmarks route; no API keys of its own, no writes outside its data directory.
entries.name: model-leaderboard

entries.description: Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $DUCKWORK_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.
entries.name: model-picker

entries.description: Explicit per-profile readiness and native missing-profile preparation; Python installation remains per profile, never automatic on refresh. Profile model settings, default-on Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads Duckwork profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background Duckwork children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — after you trust and enable the plugin, routing defaults ON for every installed profile without a saved choice, including profiles that installed an earlier version and never saved one (the update turns it on); existing saved OFF and explicit skill opt-outs remain OFF. On enabled profiles, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background Duckwork agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. The Desktop "prepare profiles" action, after you select profiles and confirm, installs and enables this same catalog pin in up to 32 other local profiles through Duckwork's plugin manager, where routing then defaults ON. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.
known_issues: v0.4.8 adds explicit local missing-profile preparation (maximum 32). Selection and known PyYAML dependency/activation consent are required, and the installed source record must match the currently resolved catalog pin. Existing, disabled, partial or custom code is manual-only; no global/future-profile auto-install or self-updater.

Native writes require an exact fresh target descriptor on the same local source; missing, duplicate, remote or aliased routes fail manual-only. Catalog lookup and profile-name binding are not atomic: do not rename/delete/recreate profiles or edit packages while preparing. Readiness observes files and effective Python selection, not existing-session registration or provider success.

Cancel/scope change stops unissued work, not an already-issued native install. Unknown outcomes are never automatically retried; both settled and unknown writes retain a settings-rebase fence until explicit owner-scoped full reload. Readiness-only refresh preserves dirty drafts; full reload discards them. Existing saved routing OFF remains OFF.

v0.4.7 also requests native completion wakes for validated default-local turns without a UI-session ID; configured-model quota can be used by continuation. Stop, busy, ownership and explicit notification opt-out remain native. Consume the owned terminal process result before reading the routed verdict; pre-consumption raw replay is not an exactly-once guarantee.

Cold PM binding selects only a verified already-imported generation; multi-argument sealed native launch layouts still fail closed. Windows noninteractive launches suppress console windows; skipped OS/permission tests do not establish other-platform coverage.

Routing is default ON after package trust/activation only for installed profiles with no saved choice. Existing OFF/skill opt-outs remain OFF; install does not rewrite models/fallback consent/budgets or launch jobs. The advanced UI retains opt-out.
Heavy/Light may use the same model in independent purpose-bound jobs. Same-model context separation does not provide different-model review diversity.
Native YAML and served-runtime bootstrap compatibility are verified on Windows. Existing private core imports remain a host-version compatibility risk and are reported by plugin validation.

Small bounded changes stay with Main. Ordinary implementation delegation requires two substantive independent workstreams with net parallel benefit; explicit delegation and required Heavy/independent review remain exceptions. This is guidance, not an API two-job minimum.

Preferences now live under Settings > Plugins. The main-sidebar settings row is removed; legacy /model-router bookmarks remain supported. A host supporting the public plugin-settings area is needed; no private-core or sidebar fallback is added.
The Desktop UI is Korean-first. Windows runtime/SDK/Desktop behavior has been tested; full Linux/macOS runtime support is not claimed.
Requires a Duckwork build with unified Python/Desktop packages and request/tool middleware; new Python tools may require a new session.
Fast and fallback can increase API charges or subscription-credit use. Transports bypassing the request middleware, including codex_app_server, are outside Fast inheritance coverage.
The native scanner can report CAUTION for the manual source-repair helper; routing-disabled capability probes can warn that coding_route was not registered.
Default-profile mid-run activation was not confirmed on the developer's shared backend; package installation is distinct from existing-session activation.

entries.title: Model Router

entries.description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to Duckwork's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

entries.description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via Duckwork default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file Duckwork loads into every session's system prompt) after a Duckwork approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; Duckwork and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when Duckwork cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from Duckwork config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to Duckwork's own default model through local Ollama; reads ~/.duckwork/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when Duckwork cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon that sends memory text to the Ollama endpoint at 127.0.0.1:11434 or NEXUS_OLLAMA_BASE under the model named by NEXUS_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL, nexus-memory.consolidation_model or Duckwork's model.default, which can be an Ollama cloud model), and the service keeps running after Duckwork exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Duckwork config.yaml, and the opt-in recall reranker (nexus-memory.rerank or NEXUS_RERANK=1) defaults to sending each query plus up to 20 memory snippets to that same endpoint using the provider API key it reads from config.yaml; reads ~/.duckwork/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.
entries.name: nexus

Opening a profile's latest session asks the app's own session.list RPC for that session's id (metadata only) and then opens it through the app's own openSession; no message content is read. Windows liveness uses the read-only OpenProcess/GetExitCodeProcess probe, never os.kill(pid, 0). entries.description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in Duckwork: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger, its own JSONL measurement log, and a read-only look at the profile's cron/jobs.json. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires Duckwork >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; it reads the profile's cron/jobs.json read-only (on `/offpeak-durum`, `/offpeak-kaldir` and at every session end) to count enabled queue-consumer jobs; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

entries.description: A Duckwork Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads duckwork-metrics-dash's <duckwork root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <duckwork root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through duckwork send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task. From the setup checklist's Connect GitLab step it can also adopt this profile's own login - its environment read through Duckwork' secret scope, or the host the gitlab-mr plugin names - or take a host and token typed on the page; the host goes through the plugin-settings writer and the token through Duckwork' .env credential route as OPERATIONS_GITLAB_TOKEN, and the token is never sent back to the page. No other credential store is read: a login that exists only in another profile's .env or in the glab CLI's config is typed in instead. Since 0.3.5 the plugin keeps its own metrics store: it tails <duckwork root>/metrics/requests.jsonl and moa-refs.jsonl, guardrail lines in logs/agent.log, logs/model-router-requests.jsonl and clientgate/clientgate-usage.jsonl (all read-only, offset-tracked) plus its own host probes (CPU and memory via sysctl/vm_stat or PowerShell, LM Studio's lms ps, and every five minutes the local conformance.yaml's install-stamp, launchd/scheduled-task, loopback-port and key-name checks), and reads session titles and costs from <duckwork root>/state.db and every profile's gateway_state.json (read-only), into <duckwork root>/metrics/operations.db, which this plugin alone writes and prunes to the metrics_retention_days setting (30/60/90 days or forever, chosen on the page and written through Duckwork' plugin-settings writer); duckwork-metrics-dash's metrics.db is then only a read-only fallback until the own store holds data. It probes the local metrics dashboard's /api/about (METRICS_DASH_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8899, cached five minutes) to link to it rather than duplicate it, and every Duckwork process that loads the plugin starts a daemon timer: when no kanban dispatcher tick has arrived for two minutes it runs the same sweep itself every 30 seconds (collection, alerts and, with drift_action: automatic, the fix cards), and the page says so; OPERATIONS_HEARTBEAT_TIMER=0 turns that timer off. Since 0.3.4 a failed model call is classified with the host app's own error classifier and shown with its cause and remedy commands; no new outbound call is made for that.
known_issues: On a fresh install the request, error, host and conformance sections read duckwork-metrics-dash's metrics.db (read-only) until the plugin's own store has collected; with neither present they show "unavailable".
Merge requests and the GitLab conformance standard need the GitLab host and token set in the plugin's settings (or GITLAB_HOST and GITLAB_TOKEN).

entries.title: Operations

entries.description: OptChat-style endless memory for Duckwork: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after Duckwork's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $DUCKWORK_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.
entries.name: optchat

entries.description: Independent Duckwork integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under DUCKWORK_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Duckwork' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.
entries.name: optmem-hermes

entries.description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Duckwork. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Duckwork provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Fordex Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Duckwork tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Duckwork conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Duckwork session API and kept in the browser only. The Fordex Atelier theme contains Fordex logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Fordex.
entries.name: orbit-desktop

entries.description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Fordex. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/DUCKWORK_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.duckwork-orca (DUCKWORK_ORCA_HOME), outside DUCKWORK_HOME.
entries.name: orcaslicer
entries.title: OrcaSlicer for Duckwork

entries.description: Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider Duckwork already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with Duckwork' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.
entries.name: orquehelx

entries.description: pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Disclosure — when enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; no network.

entries.description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.
entries.name: pcs-security-tls-posture

entries.description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Duckwork installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.
entries.name: pdf-surgeon

entries.description: Desktop-only, read-only monitor for pending memory and skill write approvals. Disclosure — the pane's API reads pending/memory/*.json and pending/skills/*.json under the default Duckwork root and every named profile directory beneath it (all profiles, not only the active one), and returns only counts, age buckets, oldest age, and per-item profile/subsystem/id/action/origin/created_at/age_seconds. It never returns or displays summaries, payloads, or record content; it exposes no approve, reject, or delete actions; it registers no tools, hooks, or middleware, performs no network I/O, and holds no credentials.
entries.name: pending-queue-monitor

Disclosure — automatic recall sends the first 4,000 characters of each nontrivial local prompt to app.mypenny.ai as a search query, and the agent can save notes there through penny_remember without a Duckwork approval prompt; works only in local CLI/TUI conversations (cron, subagents and gateways are refused); login is a manual command that registers its own OAuth client with clerk.mypenny.ai and briefly listens on 127.0.0.1 for the callback; tokens are kept in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/penny/auth.json (owner-only) and are not removed on uninstall; no raw transcript upload, telemetry or other-client credential reuse.
entries.name: penny
entries.title: Penny

Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

entries.name: phone-harness

Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/) with a local stdio MCP server and bundled skill; needs Node.js 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium 120+. entries.description: Email for Duckwork through Pidgeon: mail to your agent's own address starts a conversation, one per email thread, and the agent's answer goes back as a reply in that thread. The agent reads Pidgeon Firewall's clean text, mail flagged as prompt injection is held before it reaches the agent, mail whose From fails DMARC never reaches it, and the agent can only reply, never write to a new recipient. Standard library only. Disclosure — while the gateway runs it polls pidgeon.ai (or `PIDGEON_BASE_URL`) every five seconds with `PIDGEON_API_KEY` and sends the agent's answers as email replies through Pidgeon; mail from senders in `PIDGEON_ALLOWED_USERS` that passes DMARC becomes agent turns with the agent's full toolset (Firewall-flagged mail is held by default; setting `PIDGEON_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true` also admits mail whose From is not authenticated, so anyone who knows an allowed address could instruct the agent), and a cursor/message-id state file is kept under `<DUCKWORK_HOME>/pidgeon/`.
entries.name: pidgeon
entries.title: Pidgeon

entries.description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

entries.description: Claude Code-style plan mode for Duckwork: the agent explores and writes a plan, and edits nothing else until you approve it. It works on every interactive Duckwork surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Duckwork tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .duckwork/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when Duckwork approvals are on, every write_file and patch then gets Duckwork' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan_profile: classic), approval_card: false and surfaces without a card use Duckwork' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions, and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, plan_profile, allow_commits and plan_skill settings). Classic CLI enforced on every supported Duckwork; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Duckwork v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 recommended. On the interactive classic CLI, Duckwork' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through Duckwork' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal Duckwork seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .duckwork/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .duckwork/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, Duckwork core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and duckwork serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file. On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write_once) it checks that Duckwork printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.
entries.name: plan-mode
entries.title: Plan mode

entries.description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under DUCKWORK_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.
entries.name: pocket-watch

entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, puts the user card and the workspace's project card in the system prompt, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Records and captured turns carry the author duckwork:<profile>. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; with the opt-in capture setting (off by default) each completed turn of the primary agent is sent too: the user's message (with the sender's display name when Duckwork knows it), the final reply, tool names and file paths, never tool output; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records (and captured turns, deleted after its message_retention_days) in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the Duckwork secret scope; the only local state is $DUCKWORK_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No threads or processes of its own (capture runs on Duckwork' sync worker), no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.
known_issues: Requires a post-cortex daemon 0.4.0 or newer; cards, authorship, capture and derived_from need 0.5.0 and are skipped on an older daemon. A daemon bound to 0.0.0.0 must list the host in the plugin URL in its allowed_hosts, or every request gets 403.
entries.name: post-cortex

entries.description: PayPerQ (ppq.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider for Duckwork — per-response cost estimation from ppq's published rate card, chat model discovery from GET /v1/models, automatic per-request Zero Data Retention opt-in, and a 3-layer picker pin strategy (user-local pins file → live top chat models from ppq's public stats dashboard → generic static fallback; generic installs never get the author's personal pins). Disclosure — model provider; PPQ_API_KEY and all prompts, tool schemas and responses go to ppq.ai (PayPerQ; terms https://ppq.ai/terms, contact matt@ppq.ai), a relay that routes requests to third-party inference partners, some outside the user's jurisdiction, and frontier providers still see prompts; usage is billed per request from the user's prepaid PayPerQ balance (funded by card or cryptocurrency on ppq.ai; the plugin itself makes no payments). Privacy protections are opt-in per request: for models badged privacyLevel 'zdr' the plugin automatically sends provider={"zdr": true, "data_collection": "deny"} so requests route only to endpoints with a Zero Data Retention policy that do not collect data (the zdr model set refreshes hourly from an unauthenticated GET /v1/models with a pinned fallback); models badged 'e2e' run inside TEE enclaves with no opt-in flag needed — enclave coverage applies to chat by default, not to image/video/audio, and true end-to-end encryption is only available via the optional local ppq-privacy-verifier proxy. Building the model picker, for any provider, starts a background unauthenticated POST to stats.ppq.ai at most hourly to fetch the top chat models; cost estimates and personal picker pins read optional local files under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/ppq/ (prices.json, pins.json) that the plugin does not create, so costs show as unknown without a price snapshot. Additional caveats: Claude Opus 4.8 with web search enabled drops the ZDR guarantee, and some Anthropic/Gemini models may override the provider routing fields (order/only/ignore).
entries.name: ppq

entries.description: Checks cold email against the law before it goes out: when the agent sends an email with a send tool, one of Duckwork's email skills (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace) or an email API call, Precleared checks each new recipient against UK PECR and UK GDPR, US CAN-SPAM, Canada's CASL and German, French, Australian, Irish and Dutch rules; anything not cleared goes to Duckwork's approval prompt (or is refused in block mode) with the rule, its source and a signed receipt. Adds precleared_check and precleared_verify_receipt tools and a cold-email-check skill. Disclosure — when the agent sends email through a send tool, an email skill (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace), a mailer command or an email-API call, and on every precleared_check call, the plugin sends each new recipient's address with the configured sender country, address source, pitch and optional prospect country to precleared.dev over HTTPS; Precleared keeps a signed receipt of each check that anyone holding the receipt id can open at precleared.dev/r/<id>. The optional PRECLEARED_API_KEY is read through Duckwork's secret scope and sent only in the Authorization header; without a key, checks draw on a free allowance shared by everyone on the same network. Emails not cleared go to Duckwork's approval prompt (or are refused in block mode), and verdicts are cached under hashed addresses in plugin state for 30 days. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry; maintained by the operator of Precleared.
entries.name: precleared
entries.title: Precleared

entries.description: Larger or smaller text in the Duckwork Desktop file preview pane: scales the rendered Markdown from 90% to 175%, independent of Chat Text Size and UI Scale, through a row in Settings → Appearance, three command-palette entries and rebindable shortcuts (⌘⌥=, ⌘⌥-, ⌘⌥0 on macOS; unbound by default on Windows and Linux, where Ctrl+Alt is AltGr). The Source and Diff views keep their size. Disclosure — desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); appends one stylesheet that sets CSS zoom on the preview's [data-preview-markdown] element, removed on disable, so a Desktop release that renames that attribute turns the plugin into a no-op; stores the chosen size in plugin storage; no network calls, credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry.
entries.name: preview-text-size
entries.title: Preview Text Size

entries.description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.
entries.name: pricewin

entries.description: Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel ask for Duckwork approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, and when those checks cannot run. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running duckwork tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" adds one unused line to config.yaml, and that line does not approve the next move. The optional watch is a cron job you create from the CLI (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. The watch needs plugins.isolation: in_process; under host it only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam.
entries.name: print-job-watch

entries.description: Turn an idea, a photo of an object, or a shop listing into a sliced Bambu Studio project. The agent writes a Blender script, print3d checks the mesh (overhangs, thin walls, fits between parts, likeness to the photo), slices it and says what to fix, until it prints clean; each run also writes a 3D view the agent opens in the Desktop preview pane. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill and a stdio MCP server run through uvx, so Blender 4.2+, Bambu Studio and uv are required; at install Duckwork looks for Blender in the standard locations (/Applications and Steam on macOS; PATH, flatpak, snap and Steam on Linux) and refuses the install without it. Disclosure — runs Blender and the Bambu Studio CLI as local child processes; Blender runs the agent-written Python with your user's permissions, outside Duckwork's terminal sandbox, and the server is marked untrusted, so Duckwork asks before every tool that runs a script or changes a job (the read-only tools still write preview images and the 3D view under ~/print3d/jobs without asking); installs Pillow and mcp from PyPI; the 3D view loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; the optional `print3d setup` command (not needed for a catalog install) edits Duckwork, Codex, Claude, Cursor and Gemini config files, with backups. Never contacts the printer; no telemetry, no credentials.
known_issues: Tested on macOS, where Blender and Bambu Studio are found automatically. On Linux, Blender must be on PATH or installed with flatpak, snap or Steam for the install to go through; set BAMBU_STUDIO_BIN if Studio is not on PATH.
Bambu Studio is not checked at install; without it, make stops at the slice step and says to install it or set BAMBU_STUDIO_BIN.
The skill folder is a symlink, so Windows is not supported.
entries.name: print3d

entries.description: The Alt+Tab gesture for Duckwork profiles. Hold Ctrl+Alt and tap Tab to cycle through your profiles, release to land on the highlighted one — the same hold-tap-release rhythm as the OS app switcher. (Alt+Tab, Win+Tab and Cmd+Tab are owned by the window manager and cannot be bound by any application, so the gesture lives on ctrl+alt+tab, unclaimed by the OS and by Duckwork core.) Each row shows the profile's model and most recent conversation; a working profile shows a spinner. Also opens with a single contributed keybind (Cmd+Alt+P / Ctrl+Alt+P, rebindable in the app's own keybind panel), a status-bar chip, and a palette command. The switch goes through the Desktop's own profile path, so the target profile's backend is activated and its chrome is scoped onto it. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network calls, or stored credentials.

entries.description: Collapses carriage-return progress bars (tqdm, git clone --progress and similar) in terminal output to the frame a terminal would show, so the model reads one line instead of every redraw: a 300-step tqdm loop goes from 17,396 characters to about 120. Other text written between redraws, CRLF line endings and output without a carriage return are left as they are. Disclosure — register() adds one transform_terminal_output hook that rewrites the output string in memory; no tools, network access, subprocesses, files, settings or environment variables.
entries.name: progress-squash

entries.description: Git workbench for the Duckwork Dashboard and Desktop: discovers the git repositories under the folders you watch, and inspects or changes them per file — stage, unstage, diff and discard — plus commit, push, pull, branches, commits and worktrees. Disclosure — reads the watch paths from its own SQLite table (under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/project-manager) and git metadata (branch, remote, ahead/behind, commit subjects, status and diff text) from the repositories under them, and lists folder names under any path you type when adding a watch folder; file contents are read only as diff text returned to the requesting UI; the five agent tools are read-only. Writes on request only from the Dashboard/Desktop UI: git add, commit, push, stash (including stash -u before a branch switch), fetch, merge --ff-only (also as "pull all" across every watched repository), restore, clean -f, git switch, and git worktree remove (including --force and remove-all). Discard on a tracked file restores it from HEAD and drops the uncommitted edits; on a file in no commit (untracked or staged-new) it leaves the bytes on disk but nothing here can restore a version of it, and both sit behind a confirmation naming which one you are doing. The Desktop Chat button starts a new Duckwork session whose working directory is that project's folder, and the project name and branch chip open the repository's remote URL in your system browser. The optional standalone server (project_manager_server.py, 127.0.0.1:9120) requires a per-run token printed to its log. No outbound network, no model call, no API keys; git fetch/push contact the remote named in the request (the UI sends the repository's own remote).

entries.description: Kanban-style prompt queue for the desktop: Play drains cards one at a time into per-card target modes — new session, existing session, project, or a profile's canonical Bot Chat — gated on the global model slot, background-review completion, and context compaction. Queue/Done/Skipped/ Failed tabs, two-row target picker, markdown ingest (Windows), and a trust-aware ::enqueue directive (ask-first by default). Disclosure — Desktop pane that runs queued prompts as full agent turns (all tools the session allows) in new or chosen existing sessions, projects it can create, or a hidden per-profile "Bot Chat" session while Play is on; reads recent agent.log lines to detect background reviews and context compaction; on Windows the markdown-ingest menu runs local shell commands (mkdir, dir, certutil, explorer, and python on a small bundled reader script it writes into the chosen folder) through Duckwork's shell.exec; an opt-in Auto-add setting lets ::enqueue directives in a live assistant reply queue prompts that run without a click.

entries.description: Flags memory and skill_manage writes that state a user decision ("the user decided ...", "用户决定 ...") without the user's own words: each such sentence needs a quote that appears verbatim in text the user typed in this session, shares key words with the decision and does not drop a negation. A patch is checked by the text it produces. Observe mode (the default) records flagged writes and `duckwork provenance-gate report` lists them; block mode refuses them and tells the model how to fix the write. Measured on an independent blind set of 133 lines: precision 1.000, recall 0.694. Disclosure — two hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call); keeps a local copy of the text the user types, with its sender_id and session link, and an evidence log of checked claims under plugin-data/provenance-gate (30-day default retention, `duckwork provenance-gate purge`); reads MEMORY.md, USER.md and skill files to reproduce what a patch produces; no network, no credentials, never asks for approval.
entries.name: provenance-gate
entries.title: Provenance Gate

entries.description: Copy provider API keys (and provider base-URL overrides) from one profile onto other profiles — a one-time, explicit copy from a desktop page. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate Duckwork environment keys on exhaust, and an expired OAuth token asks for a new login. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent. When the Discord gateway runs, the bot's Discord presence (visible to everyone in servers the bot shares) is updated every 20 seconds by default with tokens/sec, context-window use and the active provider's name with its remaining quota or dollar credit balance (model and running tool are opt-in); turn it off with plugins.entries.provider-status.settings.discord_presence_enabled: false. /pulse and the agent_pulse tool report process-wide telemetry (model, provider, current tool, quota) to anyone allowed to call them on a gateway. Writes a secret-free quota-cache.json into its install folder and reads Duckwork config.yaml for the active model.

entries.description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Duckwork desktop status bar. Providers: OpenCode Go, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Fordex, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured. No subprocesses, no telemetry.

Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account (fails closed); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions and wait in ~/.pushary/run/duckwork-commands; sends session events with a machine id (~/.pushary/machine-id when present, else a hashed hostname) on every turn, the redacted command and description of each approval it carries, the redacted reason when Duckwork marks a turn failed (max 200 characters), redacted gated-tool arguments and pushary_remind reminder text to pushary.com; reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through Duckwork.
