entries.description: Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, Duckwork's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands, the command waiting on the sudo password prompt (redacted by Duckwork; never the password) and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $DUCKWORK_HOME/logs and settings.json under $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data, and $DUCKWORK_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. Outbound-only, no inbound or approval path, no telemetry, no background processes.
entries.name: pushover-hermes-plugin

entries.description: Durable native memory for Duckwork with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the Duckwork-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update and qdrant_memory_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and `migrate mem0` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — memory text is stored in the configured Qdrant store (embedded files under <DUCKWORK_HOME>/qdrant-memory/qdrant by default, or the Server/Cloud URL you set), and memory text plus each turn's recall query are sent as plain text to the configured embedding endpoint (default local Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434; an OpenAI-compatible remote endpoint can be configured, and keyed endpoints must use HTTPS). Disclosure — after each primary-agent turn, at session end and before context compression, conversation text goes to the LLM configured in Duckwork through the Duckwork plugin LLM facade (a provider/model override needs the plugin's Duckwork trust grant) to extract facts and to compare near-duplicate memories; that LLM may be a remote provider. Disclosure — the provider is selected with memory.provider: qdrant-memory; its settings live in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/qdrant-memory.json (0600, secrets stripped on save). QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_API_KEY are read through the Duckwork secret scope, but an api_key written by hand into qdrant-memory.json takes precedence, and `migrate mem0` reads the source Qdrant endpoint and any api_key from <DUCKWORK_HOME>/mem0.json or --source-config. Disclosure — state lives under <DUCKWORK_HOME>/qdrant-memory/ (embedded store, SQLite WAL ledger, lock files); the ledger holds raw turn text and pre-compression transcripts until they are processed, and failed items until retried, then scrubs the bodies. Disclosure — single-writer design: a local ownership lock excludes a second writer to the same profile destination, and Server/Cloud deployments expect one active writer per scope. Disclosure — deletion removes records and fences pending operations, but is not a forensic secure erase (SQLite WAL pages and backups may retain content).
known_issues: Preview scope: multi-writer Server/Cloud deployments, hybrid retrieval and a web UI are not supported.
Deletion removes records and fences pending operations but is not a forensic secure erase; storage-level remnants (WAL, backups) may persist.
Embedded mode is single-writer: a second process fails closed on the ownership lock instead of sharing the store.
Extraction adds LLM latency after a turn; memory admission is not guaranteed before the host admits the provider, and pending operations replay on the next start.
entries.name: qdrant-memory

entries.description: Dense semantic memory for Duckwork, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off | summary | verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off | minimal | verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Duckwork secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <DUCKWORK_HOME>/qdrant-status.json. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.duckwork/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/duckwork_default, ~/.duckwork/duckwork-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base Duckwork home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate duckwork_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Duckwork process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's Duckwork session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it.
known_issues: Windows on ARM is unsupported: grpcio, pulled in by qdrant-client, has no win_arm64 wheel. Linux and macOS on x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 are supported.
Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported — the provider is REST-only and requires a reachable server.

md_search returns 'no markdown index yet' until you run the bundled ingest script once (python scripts/md_ingest.py, lexical only and fast; add --semantic for the embedding tier, which takes about 7 minutes for 5500 chunks on a 5-core CPU). No background process does this for you.

Running the plugin's pytest suite inside an installed copy still changes the PM dependency stamp (the .pytest_cache directory is hashed as a build input); only an upstream core change can exclude gitignored state.
entries.name: qdrant

entries.description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the duckwork-quota-plugin User-Agent, caching Anthropic usage responses and rate-limit cooldowns in the Duckwork root directory keyed by a token hash so profiles sharing one Claude login share them; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from Duckwork' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; when a Codex account is configured, each refresh also fetches public Codex reset announcements from the third-party site codex-resets.com (anonymous request, no credentials sent); the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, Duckwork' auth.json pool and OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check first sends Duckwork' own xai-oauth access token (read via Duckwork or from auth.json, read-only) to grok.com's billing endpoint with a browser User-Agent, and on an authentication failure falls back to local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux, the macOS Keychain or Windows DPAPI for the browser's cookie key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or every saved commandcode credential in Duckwork' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA_API_KEY from ~/.duckwork/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage, /api/balance and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from Duckwork' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints. The opt-in (default off) Agent Monitor reads this profile's Duckwork session database and the local process list to show running sessions, spend estimates and model health, locally only.
entries.name: quota

entries.description: Codex-style ask-about-selection for Duckwork Desktop: select text anywhere in a conversation, and a small pill appears above the selection offering Quote & ask — the selection lands in the message composer as a Markdown quote with the caret on the line below, ready for your question — or Copy, which puts the same Markdown quote on the clipboard. A command-palette entry does the same without the pill. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, nothing written to disk, nothing persisted. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; serializes the selection to Markdown (fenced code with its language, nested lists, bold/italic, links), cut at 4000 characters; writes the draft through host.composer (getDraft/setDraft, falling back to insertText, then ctx.os.writeClipboard) and focuses the composer; ignores selections made inside the composer itself and hides on collapse, scroll or Escape. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.
entries.name: quote-ask
entries.title: Quote & Ask

entries.description: A quotum seat's Venice key as a provider. Private and anonymized models, with the seat's daily cap, spend and the 20:00 UTC bell in /usage, and a Seals tab in duckwork dashboard with the seat's record. Disclosure — prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY go to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage and the Seals tab send a 16-hex sha256 handle of the key to quotum.org, then the Seals tab reads the seat's public record from quotum.org (the key itself is never sent there); QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 swaps in its own client that drops Duckwork web_search for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token
known_issues: The optional QUOTUM_X_SEARCH mode supplies its own client through create_client, so it works with plugins.isolation in_process (the default) only; under host isolation leave it off.
Duckwork' bundled Achievements page has no hook for outside achievements, so the seat's seals live in the plugin's own Seals tab.
entries.name: quotum

entries.description: Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC_ALLOWED_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until duckwork tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until duckwork cron remove. Duckwork main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project.
entries.name: radio-dm-gateway

entries.description: Inspect captured browser verification evidence locally when an agent task is interrupted by a CAPTCHA. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (pinned stateless mcp.json + skill); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ with npx on PATH. Disclosure — on first start Duckwork runs `npx rea-captcha@0.3.1`, which downloads that exact npm package and its dependencies (incl. Playwright) from the npm registry; the catalog config is stateless, so only the read-only, local captcha_analyze works and the browser-session tools fail closed until you configure a separate stateful server; no telemetry, hosted solver, browser-profile copying, or cookie/token transfer.
entries.name: rea-captcha

entries.description: Reverse engineer programs with REA (rea.tools): native binaries, .NET assemblies, Electron/JavaScript apps, Android packages, firmware and browser/process activity, through REA's MCP server (pinned rea-agents@6.7.0 over npx stdio) with REA's reverse-engineer-anything skill adapted for Duckwork. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ on PATH, plus your own Ghidra, Hopper or IDA for native decompilation. Disclosure — a few REA tools run a command under a PTY, launch or drive an application, change a connected Android device or overwrite a chosen file, and Duckwork does not prompt before them; the bundled skill tells the agent to ask first and to skip them in unattended runs.
entries.name: rea

entries.description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (always returns None, so dispatch is never changed), pre_llm_call and gateway_platform_event hooks; keeps a bounded in-memory record of private-chat message ids, 60-character excerpts and reactions; writes nothing to disk, makes no network requests, starts no processes and reads no secrets.
entries.name: reaction-feedback

entries.description: Local ledger of the emoji reactions people leave on messages in your Telegram chats with Duckwork: /reaction-log counts each message once, with the reactions it has now, and shows per emoji how many messages carry it, in how many chats and how long ago it was last set, or per day with the day's most used emoji, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, or everything recorded; /reaction-log recent lists the newest reaction changes (ten, or up to 100 with /reaction-log recent 50). Only reactions the gateway authorizes reach it. Disclosure — subscribes to gateway_platform_event as an observer only and ignores every event but a reaction change; writes the emoji a message has after the change, a count of custom emoji and 12-digit hashes of the chat and message ids (never a user id, user name or message text) to plugin-data/reaction-ledger/reactions.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network
entries.name: reaction-ledger

entries.description: Local-first WeRead (微信读书) reading companion: syncs bookshelf, reading stats and notes to the local machine and turns them into private reading cards and weekly/monthly reviews through 8 MCP tools, with a built-in fictional demo mode for previews. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (e5f6673) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 20+ on PATH. All data stays in PLUGIN_DATA; never posts to WeRead — cards and reviews are local files saved only after user confirmation. Disclosure — live mode sends your WEREAD_API_KEY as a Bearer token plus book ids and paging cursors to i.weread.qq.com (Tencent's WeRead agent gateway) and nothing else; the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first; the engine's npm dependencies resolve as caret ranges at first launch.
entries.name: reading-buddy

entries.description: Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.
entries.name: reasoning-switch

entries.description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop
entries.name: recency-anchor

entries.description: Teaches Duckwork's built-in secret redactor 71 more vendor credential formats (HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, Amazon Bedrock, Atlassian, Cloudflare, Supabase, Tailscale, Docker Hub, JFrog Artifactory, CircleCI, HubSpot, PostHog, Grafana, Sentry, Shopify and others) through register_redaction_patterns, so those tokens are masked in logs, tool output and model-bound text like the built-in ones. Disclosure — register() makes one call, ctx.register_redaction_patterns; no tools, hooks, network access, subprocesses, files or environment variables; the patterns can only add masks, and security.redact_secrets: false still turns redaction off.
entries.name: redaction-pack

entries.description: Guided Markdown and source-code review in Duckwork Desktop — annotate passages or line-numbered code in a docked pane and send comment/question/change-request batches back to the agent; cards are offered automatically on delivered Markdown. Disclosure — reads any user-selected local .md/.markdown or source-code path (.py .sh .js .ts .tsx .c .h .cpp .go .rs .rb .yaml .yml .json .toml .sql, so config files such as config.yaml or auth.json are shown if you open them) up to 1 MB (symlink-resolved), writes only a <file>.redline.json sidecar beside it, and in Duckwork Desktop chats the transform_llm_output hook appends a ::redline directive line to qualifying final agent responses; syntax highlighting uses Pygments in the local gateway host with plain-text fallback; no network beyond the local gateway, no credentials, no telemetry, no subprocesses; the pane polls the local backend every 3 s while open.
entries.name: redline

entries.description: Detects when a model refuses a request or deflects to an educational alternative, and retries the turn on the next model in your fallback_providers chain; optionally appends your own text to the retry's system prompt after a refusal. Detection is local and rule-based (regex patterns over the response prose); tool-calling responses, code blocks and partial answers are treated as genuine answers. Disclosure — an llm_execution middleware inspects every model response before the agent loop uses it, and when it detects a refusal it sets finish_reason to content_filter (Anthropic: stop_reason to refusal) so Duckwork activates its fallback model; this is logged and counted identically to a real provider-signalled refusal (reason=content_policy_blocked), with no way for a plugin to register a distinct reason, so the detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id to let the two be told apart by hand; a triggered fallback resends the full conversation to the fallback provider and spends tokens there; with no fallback provider configured, Duckwork replaces the response with its standard safety-refusal notice, so a false positive discards a valid answer. Optional (off by default, empty preprompt/preprompt_escalated settings): an llm_request middleware appends your configured text to the system prompt of requests in an armed session, so a same-route retry of the same model carries it; armed state is memory-only unless persist_state is enabled, in which case session ids/levels/turn ids (never text or credentials) are kept in Duckwork's plugin state. No network calls, no files read or written outside the plugin package (and, if persist_state is on, its own plugin-data file), no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry sent anywhere.
known_issues: Detection is pattern-based, so an unusual refusal phrasing can be missed and a response that quotes refusal language can occasionally be flagged. Configure at least one fallback model so a false positive does not discard an answer.

A detected refusal appears under Duckwork's own content_policy_blocked failover reason, identically to a real provider-signalled refusal; plugins cannot register a distinct reason (duckwork-agent#138900). The detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id so the two can be correlated and told apart by hand, but no plugin can fix Duckwork's own aggregate counts.

The optional preprompt (off by default) rewrites the system prompt of the retry. Duckwork skips a fallback entry that resolves to the same provider+model as the one that just failed, so retrying the SAME model needs a different route to it in fallback_providers (see README). This is a prompt-injection mechanism by design — read the disclosure before enabling it.
entries.name: refusal

entries.description: Reka as a Duckwork model provider: Reka's agent-capable models on Reka's OpenAI-compatible API, each with its context window, tool support and image input declared, and reasoning effort sent as Reka's top-level reasoning_effort. Pick Reka in `duckwork model` or use `--provider reka`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access); chat requests (prompts, tool schemas and results, supported user images) and the model list go to https://api.reka.ai/v1 (or REKA_BASE_URL) through Duckwork's own client with REKA_API_KEY, which Duckwork reads; usage is billed to your Reka account; the plugin itself opens no connections.
known_issues: Images inside tool results (screenshots, vision_analyze) reach the model as Duckwork's text summary. Images you attach to a message go to the models that accept them.
The model list is fixed per release. A new Reka model appears after a reviewed SHA bump.
entries.name: reka-provider
entries.title: Reka

entries.description: Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.duckwork/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.
entries.name: remarkable

entries.description: Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.
entries.name: reme

entries.description: Bounded image-to-GLB jobs using an isolated Remesher CLI, with existing ComfyUI/Comfy3D or native TRELLIS.2 and Pixal3D runtimes. Four Python SDK tools provide health, generation, persistent job status and hashed GLB assets, plus a setup/generation skill. Apache-2.0 for Remesher code; third-party terms remain separate. Disclosure — reads selected local images and configured files, uploads images to the configured ComfyUI server, launches local CLI subprocesses and detached supervisors, optionally owns a GPU runtime, and stores inputs, logs and assets in profile plugin data. Client/runtime installation and model downloads require separate explicit opt-ins; no model weights are bundled. No credentials or telemetry are required. No Desktop viewer or hosted service is included.
known_issues: Native inference tested on Linux ARM64 NVIDIA Spark only; macOS, Windows, CPU, MPS and ROCm inference are not certified.
Requires Python 3.11+, a separately installed CLI and configured runtime/model files. Native quality settings are explicit resource-intensive opt-ins, not automatic defaults.
Single-image quality remains provisional; no automatic background removal, manifold, watertightness or production-anatomy guarantee.
One active job per profile; retention is manual and native runtime logs are not size-capped. Local timeout does not cancel work on an existing remote server.
entries.name: remesher
entries.title: Remesher

entries.description: Deploy, debug and manage Render applications with 20 unchanged skills from render-oss/skills and Render's hosted MCP connection. Disclosure — connects Duckwork to Render's hosted MCP server (mcp.render.com) with your RENDER_API_KEY; the server is marked untrusted so tools without a read-only annotation need approval; account permissions apply and changes can incur Render charges; bundled skills guide shell commands, file edits and Render CLI installs (including the vendor's curl | sh installer).
known_issues: render-docker is excluded because its upstream Dockerfile cleanup example triggers a critical scanner rule.
Render's list_workspaces lacks a read-only annotation and requires approval; unattended calls are denied.
An existing native mcp_servers.render configuration overrides the package connection and trust setting.
entries.name: render-platform
entries.title: Render

entries.description: Find people and coordinate real-world work through the RentAHuman marketplace. Disclosure — runs the third-party `rentahuman-mcp` server via npx, which sends your requests and your RentAHuman API key to rentahuman.ai and stores agent identity keys in `~/.rentahuman-identities/`; its tools can post and fund tasks, accept workers, send messages and release real money to people — write-capable calls ask for approval because the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, but each approval moves money or commits you to work.

entries.title: RentAHuman

entries.description: Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.
entries.name: replaid

entries.description: Requesty LLM gateway as a Duckwork model provider (`--provider requesty`, alias `rq`, or Requesty in `duckwork model`). The picker lists Requesty's managed routing policies (curated routes with failover, `@eu` variants for EU-only hosting); any Requesty model id or org policy also works. `/reasoning` maps onto Requesty's `reasoning_effort` for reasoning-capable models, the Duckwork session id is sent as `requesty.trace_id`, and context windows and estimated cost come from the Requesty catalog. Prompt caching is done server-side by Requesty. Disclosure — chat requests go to https://router.requesty.ai/v1 (or REQUESTY_BASE_URL) through Duckwork' own client with REQUESTY_API_KEY, which Duckwork reads; the plugin itself only fetches Requesty's public model catalogs (/v1/models/managed and /v1/models, no credentials), once per process, sometimes on a short-lived background thread. No attribution headers, telemetry, file access or processes. Supersedes #27908.

entries.description: @rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

entries.description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Duckwork Agent. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a Duckwork dependency) — no extra packages needed.
entries.name: rocketchat-platform

entries.description: rply gateway platform: talk to Duckwork from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach Duckwork as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server Duckwork' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `duckwork rply` setup command; credentials read through Duckwork' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.
entries.name: rply-platform
entries.title: rply

entries.description: Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.
entries.name: rss-reader

entries.description: Community plugin that rewrites Duckwork terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local), so a Docker or remote backend without rtk never receives an rtk command. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Duckwork host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.
entries.name: rtk-rewrite-docker

entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Duckwork terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/duckwork/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).
entries.name: rtk-rewrite

entries.description: RuAPI as Duckwork model providers on one key: `ruapi` serves Claude models over RuAPI's native Anthropic Messages API (so Duckwork' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `ruapi-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi and other chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, leaving out image and video models, and context windows and image input are declared for the main models. Maintained by RuAPI. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and RUAPI_API_KEY go to https://www.ruapi.ai (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Duckwork' own clients, and RuAPI forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Duckwork' standard GET https://www.ruapi.ai/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.
entries.name: ruapi
entries.title: RuAPI

entries.description: Build, run and test Python in an offline container per chat, with results as a plain file:line issue list. The agent syncs files or folders in as copies, then runs run (a shell command), check (ruff error rules) and test (pytest); fixes stay in the box until the user asks for export, which writes changed files back through write_file and reports host files changed since the sync as conflicts. In Duckwork Desktop a VS Code-style editor opens beside the chat: file tabs with in-place editing, Run / Check / Test / Stop, and PROBLEMS / OUTPUT / RUNS panels that follow the agent live. Ships the runbox:dev-loop starting-point skill. Disclosure — needs Docker (on macOS a dedicated colima profile 'runbox', started on demand with --activate=false and its own Docker config); pulls the container image pinned by digest and installs a hash-pinned checker toolchain (ruff 0.16.9, pytest 9.1.1 and deps) from PyPI once per image; the work container has no network, hardened flags, and runs commands without Duckwork' dangerous-command approval like Duckwork' Docker backend; install (PyPI) always asks for approval in a separate installer container; a write_file/patch on an imported original asks for approval (guard_imports); export reads each existing target through read_file before replacing it; a background thread removes idle containers (15 min), stops the VM, and removes boxes of deleted or long-idle chats (reads state.db read-only hourly); adds a short per-turn note (about 80 tokens); no credentials or telemetry.
known_issues: Needs Docker: on macOS install colima and the docker CLI (brew install colima docker); on Linux a running Docker daemon. The first start on macOS downloads the VM image and takes a few minutes.
The Duckwork data folder must be under your home folder on macOS (colima shares only that).
The agent may not always pick runbox on its own (the model chooses its tools). Ask it to use runbox.
entries.name: runbox
entries.title: runbox

entries.description: Runcrate (runcrate.ai) open models via the OpenAI-compatible API at api.runcrate.ai/v1: live model list from /v1/models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default, and Duckwork reasoning settings sent as reasoning_effort. Disclosure: model provider; prompts, tool schemas and RUNCRATE_API_KEY go to api.runcrate.ai, and free requests can be served by third-party model providers under their own terms (runcrate.ai/privacy).
entries.name: runcrate-provider
entries.title: Runcrate

entries.description: Source 2 documentation and mod tooling for CS2 and Deadlock from a local index of Valve's own game data: convars, Hammer entities with their inputs and outputs, schema classes and enums, game events, the cs_script and Pulse APIs and Source2Wiki pages, plus the mod pipeline — scaffold addons, validate scripts and .cfg files, start map builds on a registered Windows host over SSH, deploy and verify hashes, and record evidence, test runs and job state. entries.description: Talk to Duckwork from Salesforce Chatter: @mention the bot user in a post or comment, it Likes the message as an acknowledgement and replies in the same thread, keeping the thread as one session. Images and files on the post are passed to the model; MEDIA files are attached back. Community plugin, not affiliated with Salesforce. entries.description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, protected hosted payment-field filling, nested HTTPS verification codes/passcodes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, secure_env_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Explicit parent payment/nested-code targeting requires compatible host task/profile ownership and browser-generation evidence and fails closed without it; this is not a general fix for native Vault named-tab selection. Payment filling requires separate native consent and exact document/control guards; explicit resume requires existing nonempty values to match Vault. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.

entries.description: Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — Duckwork installs the declared `python-socks[asyncio]` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by Duckwork) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass Duckwork allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a Duckwork approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<DUCKWORK_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native Duckwork messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.
known_issues: After updating, restart the backend used by Desktop and the gateway; a new chat alone may still use older loaded plugin code.
Preview: Windows Desktop sign-in was previously confirmed; automatic MCP appearance still needs a Desktop UI check, and a real Senler Relay workflow needs end-to-end verification.
Requires current Duckwork with native MCP OAuth and Relay transport; gateway proxy mode and multiplexed profiles are unsupported.
Monitoring notifications require a connected messaging channel; arbitrary Desktop/TUI chats are unsupported.

entries.description: A search window over your Duckwork session history, opened with Cmd+Option+F, from the command palette, or from the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover shows the chord. The empty box lists pinned then recent sessions, the preview pane shows the matching message with its neighbours, and the footer carries the round trip in whole milliseconds. It reads the session database read only, registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware, needs no credentials or environment variables; its only network calls are the loopback checks named below. Disclosure — while the search window is in use, the plugin's dashboard backend checks every 30 seconds for a separate session-find service at http://127.0.0.1:8474 (or the URL in SESSION_FIND_URL) and, when one answers, sends it your search text, preview requests and the ids of sessions you open, and shows the results it returns; otherwise it reads your Duckwork session database read-only.

entries.description: Mirrors Duckwork Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $DUCKWORK_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $DUCKWORK_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `duckwork session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $DUCKWORK_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. entries.description: Rug-pull detection for installed agent skills — fingerprints every file in every skill directory (SHA-256), keeps a profile-local snapshot, and reports exactly which skill files changed, appeared, or vanished since; a skill that mutates after install without the user touching it is the rug-pull signal. A skill directory made unreadable is reported as a finding, never treated as clean. Read-only observer, stdlib-only, zero network calls; blind spots (oversize files, symlinks, permission-denied) are counted and printed, never silent. The wrapper registers an hourly pre_llm_call hook that injects findings into the agent context, plus a /skill-integrity slash command (snapshot | check | show) that creates the baseline snapshot and shows the file-level diff. The CLI supports --state-dir to target the plugin's manifest directly. Skill dirs and state derive from get_duckwork_home(), covering non-default profiles. Disclosure — reads (hash-only, read-only) every file under the active profile's skills directory and ~/.claude/skills, stores a mode-0600 snapshot in DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/skill-integrity, and at most hourly injects the names of changed skills into the agent's context.
entries.name: skill-integrity

entries.description: Records where each skill version's content came from, so a skill that rewrites itself can be audited afterwards. For every skill write — a foreground skill_manage call, a background-review edit, or a curator consolidation — it stores the skill content fingerprint before and after, the sources present earlier in the same session (the text the user typed, tool results such as a fetched page or a file, and skills that were read), how each source is linked to the added lines — strong (at least three shared 8-word shingles), anchor (a shared operative token: a URL or host, a shell command with its first argument, a package install, a file path, an environment variable, an IP or e-mail address, that is not common across sources), or context (seen in the session, nothing measurable shared; recorded, not followed by default) — and a seq -> prev_hash -> hash chain over the entries. Text is never stored: hashes are keyed per install and the key stays in plugin-data/skill-lineage. `duckwork skill-lineage trace <skill>` shows where the newest version came from, `descendants <url|skill>` lists every skill a source produced, `report` lists versions carrying operative lines of no traceable origin, `verify` re-walks the chain, and `head` prints a value to record elsewhere so a later `verify --head` can tell truncation from an intact chain; a key reset is recorded in the chain and shown in `status` rather than happening silently. The plugin does not stop a write and does not judge a skill: it records and it verifies, and it does not claim a source caused an edit. Prior work on memory lineage (MemLineage, arXiv:2605.14421) is acknowledged in the README. Measured on 2026-10-22 against Duckwork 3166d61: Python 3.14 62 passed; Python 3.11 54 passed, 1 skipped; `duckwork plugins validate` reports no warning other than one known false positive (a test template that quotes a "curl | sh" instruction as data and never runs it). Evaluation (generated scenarios and 120 real-model runs) in the README; raw output in eval/. A manual end-to-end run in an isolated DUCKWORK_HOME (one real session creating a skill through skill_manage, then status/trace/descendants/report/verify/head) passed, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-10-21.txt. Disclosure — four read-only hooks (on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call); reads tool results, user messages and skill files (in this profile, every other profile's skills folder, the project's .duckwork/skills and the skills.external_dirs it reads from config.yaml) to compute keyed hashes; keeps hashes (no text) for 7 days per session and the lineage chain (hashes and skill names) under plugin-data/skill-lineage; no network, no credentials, never blocks or changes a tool call.
entries.name: skill-lineage
entries.title: Skill Lineage

entries.description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $DUCKWORK_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.
