entries.description: Local ledger of the turns you stopped while Duckwork was still working (/stop, or /new and /reset during a running turn, on messaging platforms, the TUI and the desktop app): /stop-log shows how many running turns were stopped, how many by /stop and by /new, in how many sessions and how long ago the last one was, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /stop-log recent lists the newest stops (ten, or up to 100 with /stop-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes stop metadata (platform, /stop or /new, Duckwork's label for the stop, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no session key or chat content) to plugin-data/stop-ledger/stops.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay or undo a stop; no network
entries.name: stop-ledger

entries.description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through Duckwork's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.
entries.name: storm-fusion-research

entries.description: How fast each model starts answering and how fast it writes: /speed shows the median and p90 time to first text and the median characters per second per model, provider or day, or lists the newest streams (ten, or up to 100 with /speed recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded, from the streaming hooks. Disclosure — writes per-response stream timings (ids, model, timings, character count, no text) to plugin-data/stream-speed/streams.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; atexit waits up to 1 s; no network
entries.name: stream-speed

entries.description: Puts the names a speech-to-text model mis-hears into the transcription prompt Duckwork sends with each voice message: terms you list (globally or per surface) and names found in this profile's memories/USER.md and MEMORY.md, most important last, within the 896 characters Duckwork keeps for Whisper-family backends; your stt.prompt stays in front. Notes written in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese or Turkish can be named in the languages setting. Disclosure — register() adds one pre_transcription hook that returns a new prompt string; memory-derived names go only to local backends (faster-whisper, local_command) unless allow_remote is set, and the memory files are not read otherwise; reads at most 256 KB per memory file; no tools, network access, subprocesses or writes; Duckwork uploads the prompt with the audio to the configured STT provider.
entries.name: stt-vocab

entries.description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.
entries.name: sugar

entries.description: Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run Duckwork. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a Duckwork approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.
entries.name: sunshine-moonlight
entries.title: Sunshine / Moonlight

entries.description: Local-first long-term memory for Duckwork, kept on your own computer: recall before each turn, tool-outcome logging, opt-in turn capture, 16 skills and /slm commands. Disclosure — talks only to the `superlocalmemory` MCP server you configure and grant in `plugins.entries.superlocalmemory.mcp_allowlist` (on this computer, or on another one with `connection: remote`): each turn's user message (redacted) is sent for recall and every tool call's arguments and result (redacted, up to 2,000 characters each) are logged to it, and with `capture_turns` on every turn is saved; `/slm` commands run the local `slm` CLI, including ones that change SLM and host settings (`/slm upgrade-hosts --apply` writes the plugin's grant into Duckwork config.yaml); `slm_agent` starts a child agent that inherits the parent session's tools.
known_issues: Grant the plugin its memory server after install: slm upgrade-hosts --host duckwork --apply (adds mcp_allowlist: [superlocalmemory]).
entries.name: superlocalmemory
entries.title: SuperLocalMemory

entries.description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.
entries.name: supermemory

entries.description: Marketplace-aware LLM routing for Surp — live prices for all models, provider TPS and trusted flags, mid-chat seller switching, secret masking, and approval-gated paid chat. Disclosure — the messages passed to surp_chat and SURP_API_KEY go to the surp.ivc.lol gateway, run by the individual developer ivcained (operator page https://surp.ivc.lol/operator, terms https://surp.ivc.lol/terms; not affiliated with Surplus Intelligence), which forwards them to third-party sellers on the Surplus Intelligence marketplace, including sellers not flagged trusted unless trusted_only is set; paid surp_chat calls spend from the user's prepaid Surp balance (USDC on Base, 5 % gateway markup), each behind a per-model Duckwork approval prompt (denied in cron and other unattended runs by default) plus a per-request ceiling (max_spend_usd, default $0.05); the price, provider, quote, combo and cache tools call the same gateway without a key; routing preferences are stored under DUCKWORK_HOME/cache/surp-duckwork-x402-llm/.
entries.name: surp-hermes-x402-llm

entries.description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. No Plug Mini on/off. Locks off unless enabled. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. Every command asks for Duckwork approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Duckwork gateway can request a command and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. Not tested on real devices. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.
entries.name: switchbot-control

entries.description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for Duckwork Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.
entries.name: t3-code-theme
entries.title: T3 Code Theme

entries.description: Document lifecycle for agents in one package: create .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf/.odt/.ods/.odp from structured JSON or raw HTML/CSS, convert between formats via pandoc + LaTeX, and read any document — anydoc (Rust, office formats and text PDFs to Markdown, in-process) with LiteParse + Tesseract OCR fallback for scanned PDFs and images, plus PDF text editing with output-directory guards. Ships as an Agent Plugins v1 package (auto-discovered plugin.json + mcp.json declaring a stdio MCP server — the client spawns it per the v1 lifecycle, PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA injected — plus an optional self-host streamable-HTTP server; first run of either bootstraps the dependency venv). The HTTP lane binds to 127.0.0.1 only and requires Bearer auth out of the box: a random token is generated into PLUGIN_DATA on first run (TABELLA_TOKEN overrides); requests with an Origin header or a non-JSON body are rejected, and model-supplied HTML cannot fetch network or local-file resources (data: URIs only — the same fetcher now also guards CSS input, not just HTML). Pandoc invocations are argument-safe: extra_args is allowlisted (--toc, --number-sections, -V key=value) and from_format/to_format are validated against the built-in format-name grammar (^[a-z0-9_]+([+-][a-z0-9_]+)*$), closing pandoc's *.lua reader/writer code-exec path; both servers re-exec into the dependency venv after bootstrap. Disclosure — Python deps (python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, weasyprint, odfpy, Pillow, lxml, PyMuPDF, firecrawl-anydoc, liteparse — 10 direct packages, transitives included in a 25-package closure) are pinned to exact versions with sha256 hashes in requirements-pinned.txt and installed with --require-hashes into a venv under PLUGIN_DATA or ~/.venvs/docs (scripts/setup.sh on Linux/macOS; on Windows the venv is built with the standard library's venv module — no bash or MSYS2 needed); system pandoc is required for conversion, a TeX engine (e.g. texlive-xetex) only when the output format is PDF (weasyprint for HTML->PDF); OCR needs the tesseract binary (UB-Mannheim build on Windows); all conversion, reading, OCR and PDF editing run locally with no network or telemetry; nothing is uploaded; read, convert, and PDF-edit tools access exactly the filesystem paths you pass; doc_create_document additionally containment-checks its output paths against the configured output directory (escape warns). Linux and Windows are CI-tested platforms (five-lane smoke battery on windows-latest: stdio lifecycle through a natively bootstrapped venv, create, read, pdf-from-html via the GTK runtime, pandoc convert).
entries.name: tabella

entries.description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs Duckwork hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.
entries.name: tailgate

entries.description: Extends Duckwork Agent API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the Duckwork API server (cross-session history search, rewind/branch/compress of API sessions, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata (no message bodies) in $DUCKWORK_HOME/talaria/observations.db; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.
entries.name: talaria-webui

entries.description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: Duckwork provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside DUCKWORK_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; duckwork memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.
entries.name: tam

entries.description: Grow a local TamaDuckwork pet from real Duckwork agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $DUCKWORK_HOME only; the optional python -m tamaduckwork CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.
entries.name: tamahermes

entries.description: Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_expand tool brings back the exact original. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Subclasses Duckwork's built-in ContextCompressor and overrides its private prune/demote methods (checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens Duckwork's re-prune runway. Adds a model-callable tameru_expand tool that returns pruned tool output from memory or from this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process. No network calls; the render log is off by default.
known_issues: Full archive recovery requires plugins.isolation to be in_process; host mode limits recovery.
Overrides private ContextCompressor signatures and falls back when the host contract changes.
entries.name: tameru
entries.title: Tameru

entries.description: Search, extract, map, crawl, and research through Tavily hosted MCP, with Tavily skills. The default connection requires TAVILY_API_KEY; supports Duckwork-managed OAuth through a native MCP override. Disclosure — Connects to Tavily's hosted MCP server at `mcp.tavily.com` and sends it the search queries, URLs and research prompts the agent issues, authenticated with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or a Duckwork-managed Tavily OAuth sign-in.
entries.name: tavily-plugin
entries.title: Tavily

entries.description: TeamoRouter as Duckwork model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so Duckwork' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Duckwork' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: duckwork-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes.
entries.name: teamorouter
entries.title: TeamoRouter

entries.description: Telegram client pane for Duckwork Desktop: dialogs, message history with image previews and per-post image reload, forum topics, and reviewed send/reply/save/delete/mark-as-read actions via a dedicated Telethon user session (separate from the core gateway bot token). All history is sanitized before rendering. Disclosure — the profile dashboard backend reads dialogs and message history and downloads media for in-page previews (page byte-budgeted and cached in memory); TELEGRAM_API_ID/TELEGRAM_API_HASH come from the profile's Duckwork secrets; login challenges stay in process memory; the dedicated Telethon session lives in DUCKWORK_HOME/telegram-plugin-auth/ (directory 0700, .session and its -wal/-shm sidecars 0600), and anyone holding that session file controls the Telegram account; delete removes the selected message for everyone; mutations go prepare -> exact preview -> confirm -> commit -> readback, and the pane's "Confirm actions" switch (on by default) can turn the preview step off; message links open in the system browser (http and https only).
entries.name: telegram-client
entries.title: Telegram Client

entries.description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Duckwork agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under DUCKWORK_HOME/telegram-notify.
entries.name: telegram-notify

entries.description: Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, read through Duckwork' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender Duckwork answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in Duckwork. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max_learned_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn_packs: false turns learning off). A pre_llm_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads Duckwork' sticker_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through Duckwork like any tool. Uses Duckwork functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision_tools.vision_analyze_tool, gateway.session_context.get_session_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only.
known_issues: Needs plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under plugins.isolation: host it cannot see the current chat, so it sends no stickers, learns no packs and adds no hint.

Every person the bot answers in a direct chat adds packs (up to max_learned_packs, default 100), which the agent then uses in every chat. Keep the gateway allowlist to yourself, or set learn_packs: false.
Before Duckwork 0.21.5, /stickers in Telegram only shows the status and reloads packs; the owner's other /stickers commands work in the Duckwork CLI on the server.
Where tool progress is on, Duckwork posts its progress line (such as telegram_sticker_send...) before a sticker; display.platforms.telegram.tool_progress: off hides every tool's lines in Telegram.
entries.name: telegram-stickers
entries.title: Telegram Stickers

entries.description: One pinned Telegram message with the state of your Duckwork on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, whether the agent sees its rules and whether its memory writes stand unapproved, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from Duckwork' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through Duckwork' own auth code); at most once per limits_refresh_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token Duckwork resolves (which, like any Duckwork request to xAI, may refresh that OAuth token and save it to auth.json, or clear a dead one, through Duckwork' own auth code), sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host Duckwork itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key Duckwork resolves (which, like any Duckwork key lookup without a usable key in .env or the environment, may save Duckwork' credential pool back to auth.json once when loading it changes something, e.g. a placeholder key in .env) and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a *_BOT_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of DUCKWORK_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; with a memory provider configured, the last 256 KB of the same log are also read for the engine's warnings about that provider, of which only the time and whether one says unavailable are kept; every tick DUCKWORK_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and DUCKWORK_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job_id, status, delivery_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send_path_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (_updates_received_total, _polling_generation, _polling_last_progress_monotonic, _polling_generation_started_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; every tick DUCKWORK_HOME/state.db is opened read-only the same way for the newest saved system prompt of each platform the running gateway lists in DUCKWORK_HOME/gateway_state.json, and the project context files the engine would load (.duckwork.md or DUCKWORK.md in that directory and each parent up to the git root, the AGENTS.override.md / AGENTS.md / agents.md chain from the git root down, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc; up to 4 MB each, links followed as the engine follows them) are read from the directory that prompt names (else the engine's TERMINAL_CWD or the gateway's working directory), and .duckwork.md, DUCKWORK.md and the AGENTS names also from the gateway's working directory and DUCKWORK_HOME, which may be outside DUCKWORK_HOME; to tell whether the prompt carries them as they are on disk; only a verdict, the file names, sizes and times are kept, never the prompt's or a file's text; every tick DUCKWORK_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (up to 4 MB each) are read to count their characters against the limits, the waiting writes in DUCKWORK_HOME/pending/memory and pending/skills (up to 2,000 files) for their names and times and, of the memory ones (up to 256 KB each), each add's target and length, and the time of DUCKWORK_HOME/skills/.curator_ledger.jsonl; never a notebook's, an entry's or a waiting write's text, and nothing there is written; the private duckwork_cli.version_info._cached_version_info and the signature of agent.prompt_builder._read_text_with_timeout are read from modules the gateway already imported, and nothing is called or changed on them; the release check keeps only each release's version and publication time and downloads, installs or replaces nothing; config.yaml is read through Duckwork' own YAML parser for the memory limits, switches, approval gate and provider name, skills.write_approval and each platform's skip_context_files; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (Duckwork' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest Duckwork release is read from api.github.com without a token at most once per 15 minutes (releases/latest with the last answer's ETag; the release list releases?per_page=100 only when Latest names another version); an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/.
known_issues: Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram handler factory receives the platform's native SDK client, which plugins.isolation: host does not allow; under host the plugin does not load and nothing is delivered.
entries.name: telegram_dashboard_probe
entries.title: Telegram Dashboard

entries.description: Telegram Business secretary: transcribes voice notes, round videos, and speech attachments right in the chat, with Settings and per-chat controls in Telegram's Manage Bot panel, plus opt-in text history (with import from a Telegram export), correspondence stats, and contact dossiers. Disclosure — audio goes to the STT backend Duckwork is configured with (local or external); transcript cleanup sends chat text through the host ctx.llm; opt-in dossiers send chat text through the Duckwork model task telesec_dossier (default Vercel AI Gateway to Google with zero data retention; an optional message check on the same gateway and optional Cloudflare fact extraction are off by default); an owner-sent /dossier posts that contact's stored dossier (without the owner note, but written with it) into the Business chat for the contact to read; runs local ffprobe/ffmpeg (argument lists, no shell) on attached audio; opt-in dossiers run a gateway background thread; modes, opt-in history, and dossiers are stored 0600 under DUCKWORK_HOME/data/telesec; reads only the numeric bot id prefix of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; no telemetry.
known_issues: Needs in-process plugin mode for native Telegram handlers.
Uses the undocumented host STT entrypoint tools.transcription_tools.transcribe_audio (no public plugin route yet; DuckMind/duckwork#142505).
entries.name: telesec
entries.title: Telesec

entries.description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.
entries.name: telnyx-provider

entries.description: Compare pinned Terraform provider and module versions with the public registry. Disclosure — tools are on for every Duckwork surface, including the gateway. Stop a surface with duckwork tools disable --platform <name> terraform-drift, or the plugin with duckwork plugins disable terraform-drift. Nothing is written under plugin-data/terraform-drift, and there is no key. Only the directory you name is read, and only .tf, .tf.json, and .terraform.lock.hcl. Symlinks and .. are refused, and .env, tfvars, .terraform, backend values, and hashes are not returned. The provider pin is the lock version, not the required_providers constraint. A module pin is an exact version only. GET calls only registry.terraform.io and, for a github.com source, raw.githubusercontent.com CHANGELOG.md. Redirects and proxy variables are ignored. A timeout or failed read leaves latest empty and is not called current. Semver orders versions, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0. The digest text is not sent and no cron job is created. known keeps newer versions, and omitting it does not call rows new today. There is no approval card. Before the call, name the directory and say there is no init, plan, apply, or state write. Cron, yolo, and approvals off can still run this read. MIT, no daily cap, requires Duckwork >=0.21.4.
entries.name: terraform-drift

entries.description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Duckwork venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under DUCKWORK_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.
entries.name: thomas

entries.description: TIDAL for Duckwork Agent: five tools (playback through local mpv, search, playlists, library, mixes) over the unofficial TIDAL API via tidalapi. Login is TIDAL's own PKCE login flow (duckwork tidal login) — no developer app needed. Playback runs on the Duckwork machine (mpv); TIDAL has no remote-device API like Spotify Connect. Needs a TIDAL subscription (any tier). Disclosure — unofficial TIDAL integration (community tidalapi library using TIDAL's own app client); stores your TIDAL access and refresh token in plaintext (owner-only, 0600) under $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/tidal/ and refreshes it itself; playback spawns a detached local mpv process with an IPC socket and plays audio on the Duckwork machine.

entries.description: @ts: context references that turn timestamps into readable times for the model: @ts:1729468800123 attaches the moment in UTC, in the local time zone and as ISO 8601, with its weekday, how long ago or ahead it is, the same moment in Unix seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, and its ISO week; bare numbers are read as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds by their length (or an s/ms/us/ns suffix) and the block says which; ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 dates and now work too, and up to 10 values in one reference also get the gaps between them; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's datetime; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @ts: reference provider

entries.description: Blocks token buys when true402 finds a honeypot or a rug in progress — one pre_tool_call hook in front of every trading tool, MCP server and terminal command (Base, Ethereum, BSC, Solana). Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the Duckwork approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. entries.description: Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Duckwork voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `duckwork ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.

Use fresh unique output filenames/stems: successful Duckwork delivery and same-stem Opus conversion can replace files outside the provider's no-clobber checks.

entries.description: Records each Duckwork session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

entries.description: Keeps an agent inside its subscription allowance: refuses a provider dispatch once a subscription usage window is exhausted, so an account that allows paid extra usage stops at the wall instead of spending overage. Reads the usage Duckwork already displays, holds no credentials, and never touches account or billing settings. Disclosure — refuses main-loop provider calls (including MoA turns) for the providers in `provider_keys` (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex by default) when a subscription usage window reaches `threshold_percent`, and by default (`fail_open: false`) also refuses when usage data is missing, stale, unreadable, or the guard's own config is malformed; usage is read through Duckwork's own account-usage fetcher (no credentials held, at most one read per source every 180 seconds by default) and cached in $DUCKWORK_HOME/plugin-data/usage-guard/usage.json; a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a short usage note to the next turn's context at 80% and 90% used by default, and an opt-in (off by default) `llm_request` middleware lowers an existing output-token budget near the usage limit; both read only the cache, never the network; auxiliary calls (compression, vision, titles, MoA advisors) are not gated.
known_issues: Anthropic windows: Duckwork's Anthropic fetcher scales any utilization <= 1 by 100, so a window at 0-1% can read as 100% and the guard will refuse. Fixed upstream by DuckMind/duckwork#139916; this entry's requires_duckwork rises to the release carrying it.
entries.name: usage-guard

entries.description: Secret-leak protection for Duckwork chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional duckwork-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

entries.description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call. By default only mpp_fetch is checked, and a payment made inside Duckwork HTTPX traffic is not seen. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host, port and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) and its HTTP method to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; a missing record or a vet402 outage asks for approval and is refused when nobody can answer, unless VET402_UNKNOWN=allow lets it pay; while enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

Adds a Status Board page (columns, follow-ups due, stale sessions, archive all done), triage of untracked sessions, a resume banner above the composer, a status-bar counter, a daily summary, palette commands and English/Arabic (RTL). SDK-only: session-row slots, a route, sidebar nav, status bar, composer banner, palette. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through Duckwork llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title_generation (Duckwork default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 (registered by __init__.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own Duckwork log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <DUCKWORK_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when Duckwork reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them.

entries.description: Publish a website, or share files and folders, at a live *.webly.site URL from Duckwork Agent with no account, then sign in to claim it, edit it, and publish drafts the person approves through the hosted Webly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Disclosure — MCP tool calls go to api.webly.ai/v1/mcp, sending WEBLY_API_KEY as a bearer header when it is set, and the webly server is marked untrusted so Duckwork asks before each Webly MCP tool that changes something. Its doctor command reads ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml only to see whether a webly MCP server is configured there. Publishing, deleting and replacing sites through that helper are gated by skill instructions, not by Duckwork approvals. The catalog copy has no update check.
known_issues: The Webly MCP tools need a sign-in, because a portable mcp.json cannot request OAuth: set WEBLY_API_KEY (a wb_ key from the Webly dashboard), or run `duckwork mcp add webly --url https://api.webly.ai/v1/mcp --auth oauth` then `duckwork mcp login webly`. Publishing without an account works without either.

entries.description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

entries.description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Fordex) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Duckwork through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under DUCKWORK_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Duckwork fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under DUCKWORK_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Duckwork; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Duckwork .env; the state file under DUCKWORK_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.

entries.title: WhatsApp Agent Platform

The bundled wicked-suite-mcp skill walks you through adding the author's hosted Wicked MCP server (https://mcp.wickedapi.com/mcp, 75 tools, some x402-priced); that server is a separate manual step and is not covered by this pin.

entries.description: Browse, search, read, write, upload, download, copy, move, share, delete and restore files on Yandex Disk over its REST API. Disclosure — sends every request to cloud-api.yandex.net, or to the https URL in YANDEX_DISK_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_DISK_OAUTH_TOKEN read through Duckwork; file bytes go to the upload and download hosts the API hands out, without the token; unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS leaves search out, loading the plugin sends one search request to learn whether the token may search, and yadisk_search is registered only if it may; every tool, permanent delete, emptying the bin and public share links included, is offered unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only Disk); yadisk_upload reads a local file and sends it unredacted, and yadisk_download writes one, after Duckwork' shared file-safety rules and the plugin's own: upload refuses .env files, Duckwork' credential stores, Duckwork' own directory and the home directories that hold keys and logins; download refuses credential files, Duckwork' own directory, .duckwork directories, agent instruction files such as AGENTS.md, system locations and paths outside DUCKWORK_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT; other local files are within reach; YANDEX_DISK_ROOT confines Disk paths, not local ones; an upload from a URL makes Yandex fetch that URL; file names and contents written by other people reach the agent as tool output; no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
known_issues: Every tool is offered by default, permanent delete and emptying the bin included. Set YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS to register fewer (read, download, write, share, delete, all or single tools, comma-separated; read is the README's advice for a first setup), then restart Duckwork

yadisk_search is registered only when the token's application may use Yandex Disk search; a token from a self-registered app or from Poligon usually may not, and the plugin then offers the other fourteen tools

yadisk_upload sends any other local file the Duckwork process can read, unredacted, and the write group includes upload; to keep the agent off local files, name the tools without upload and download, e.g. YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS=read,mkdir,write_file,copy,move,trash_restore
entries.name: yandex-disk
entries.title: Yandex Disk

entries.description: Yandex Search API as a backend for the built-in web_search (provider name yandex), plus a yandex_generative_search tool for grounded answers with cited sources. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
known_issues: Paid: every web_search routed to yandex and every yandex_generative_search call is billed by Yandex Cloud to the folder that owns YANDEX_API_KEY; the Search API must be enabled for that folder, with billing active

Installing does not switch web_search over: run duckwork config set web.search_backend yandex. The backend is search-only, so web_extract stays with another backend. yandex_generative_search is offered to the agent as soon as the plugin is enabled (toolset yandex_search; duckwork tools turns it off per platform)
Searches the Russian market (SEARCH_TYPE_RU) unless YANDEX_SEARCH_TYPE names another: SEARCH_TYPE_COM, SEARCH_TYPE_TR, SEARCH_TYPE_KK, SEARCH_TYPE_BE or SEARCH_TYPE_UZ

entries.title: Yandex Search API

entries.description: List, create, update, RSVP to, move and delete Yandex Calendar events over CalDAV, with attendees, busy status and several calendars. Disclosure — sends every request to caldav.yandex.ru, or to the HTTPS URL in YANDEX_CALENDAR_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_CALENDAR_LOGIN and YANDEX_CALENDAR_APP_PASSWORD read through Duckwork; all seven tools, delete included, are offered unless YANDEX_CALENDAR_ACTIONS narrows them; the tools act as your Yandex account, so adding attendees makes Yandex email each of them an invitation from you, and changing, answering, moving or deleting a meeting may notify the people on it; delete removes the event from the server and the plugin keeps no copy; event text written by other people, such as whoever invites you, reaches the agent as tool output; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
known_issues: Every tool is offered by default, yandex_calendar_delete_event included. Set YANDEX_CALENDAR_ACTIONS to register fewer (read, write, delete, all or single actions, comma-separated; read is the README's advice for a new setup), then restart Duckwork

The tools act as your Yandex account: adding attendees, to a new event or an existing one, makes Yandex email each of them an invitation from you, and changing, answering, moving or deleting a meeting may notify the people on it

Recurring events are not expanded: a series is listed as stored, with the times of its first occurrence, and one with modified occurrences can be moved or deleted but not edited or answered. A listing over 2 MiB of XML is refused with a request for a shorter range, and a recurring series counts in full
Read-only calendars such as holidays and birthdays accept a new event without storing it, and yandex_calendar_create_event still reports success: keep them out with YANDEX_CALENDAR_CALENDARS
entries.name: yandex_calendar
